title: Bringing Back the Night Sky
paragraphs: Before dawn one January morning in 1994, an earthquake cut off the electricity across Los Angeles. According to a well-known story, some people who stepped outside called a local science center to ask about a strange silver cloud in the sky. It was the Milky Way, our own galaxy, which many of them had never seen.

That cloud is still there every night, simply hidden. Street lights, signs, and buildings send light [[upward|L6-0950]], where it scatters in the air and forms a glow over cities. For [[astronomers|L6-0063]], this light pollution is a serious problem, because faint stars disappear behind the glow. But the harm reaches beyond [[astronomy|L6-0064]]. Many birds [[navigate|L6-0586]] by the stars when they travel at night, and brightly lit buildings can lead them [[astray|L6-0061]]. For humans, too much light at night can cause a [[disturbance|L6-0271]] in sleep.

The good news is that light pollution is easy to fix: it disappears the moment a light is switched off. A few simple ideas are [[applicable|L6-0051]] in almost any town: cover lights so that they shine only where needed, turn them off late at night, and choose warmer colors. In 2019, Hehuan Mountain in central Taiwan became the country's first International Dark Sky Park. On clear nights, visitors there can enjoy an [[awesome|L6-0071]] [[spectacle|L6-0845]] of stars, and young people who [[aspire|L6-0058]] to study the universe can see it with their own eyes.

If you want to watch the stars yourself, check the [[approximate|L6-0053]] time the moon rises, since its bright light hides faint stars. Once you arrive, wait [[awhile|L6-0072]]; your eyes need about twenty to thirty minutes to adjust to the dark. To spot a very faint star, [[avert|L6-0069]] your eyes slightly and look just to one side of it, because the edges of the eye are more sensitive to weak light. Some clubs give a [[badge|L6-0075]] to members who [[attain|L6-0065]] a goal such as finding twenty famous objects in the sky. A star show in a museum [[auditorium|L6-0068]] can be fun, but nothing matches the [[anticipation|L6-0048]] of waiting under a real sky as the stars slowly appear.
zh: 1994 年一月某天清晨天還沒亮，一場地震讓整個洛杉磯停電。根據一則廣為流傳的故事，有些走到戶外的民眾打電話給當地的科學中心，詢問天空中一片奇怪的銀色雲帶是什麼。那其實是銀河，也就是我們所在的星系，而其中很多人從來沒見過它。
那片「雲」其實每晚都在，只是被遮住了。路燈、招牌和建築物把光往上送，光在空氣中散射，在城市上空形成一層光暈。對天文學家來說，這種光害是個嚴重的問題，因為黯淡的星星會消失在光暈後面。但它的危害不只影響天文學。許多鳥類在夜間遷徙時靠星星辨認方向，燈火通明的建築可能讓牠們迷失方向。對人類而言，夜間光線太多也會干擾睡眠。
好消息是，光害很容易解決：燈一關，光害就消失了。有幾個簡單的做法幾乎在任何城鎮都適用：替燈具加上燈罩，讓光只照在需要的地方；深夜時把燈關掉；選用色溫較暖的燈光。2019 年，台灣中部的合歡山成為台灣第一座國際暗空公園。晴朗的夜晚，遊客可以在那裡欣賞令人讚嘆的滿天星斗，立志研究宇宙的年輕人也能親眼看見這片星空。
如果你想親自去看星星，先查好月亮大約幾點升起，因為明亮的月光會蓋過黯淡的星星。抵達之後，請等一會兒；眼睛大約需要二、三十分鐘才能適應黑暗。想看清一顆很暗的星星時，可以把視線稍微移開，看向它的旁邊，因為眼睛的周邊部位對微弱的光比較敏感。有些社團會頒發徽章給達成目標的成員，例如找到天空中二十個著名天體。在博物館的演講廳看星空節目也很有趣，但沒有什麼比得上在真正的夜空下，等待星星一顆顆浮現的那份期待。

questions.stem: What did some people in Los Angeles call a science center about in 1994?
options: Why the electricity had been cut off
A strange silver cloud in the sky
A bright light from a tall building
questions.explain: 第一段說停電後有些民眾打電話給科學中心，詢問天空中一片奇怪的銀色雲帶，其實那是銀河，故選 (B)。(A)(D) 停電和地震是事件背景，並非他們打電話詢問的內容。
questions.evidence: called a local science center to ask about a strange silver cloud in the sky

questions.stem: According to the passage, which is one way to reduce light pollution?
options: Building more science centers in cities
Covering lights so that they shine only where needed
Turning on street lights earlier in the evening
questions.explain: 第三段列出減少光害的方法：替燈具加罩讓光只照在需要的地方、深夜關燈、選用暖色燈光，故選 (C)。(B) 與「選用較暖的顏色」相反。
questions.evidence: cover lights so that they shine only where needed

questions.stem: The word "avert" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 後文接著說要「看向星星的旁邊」，因為眼睛周邊對弱光比較敏感，可知 avert your eyes 是「把視線稍微移開」，故選 (D)。(A) 閉上眼睛就什麼也看不到了。
questions.evidence: avert your eyes slightly and look just to one side of it

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Light pollution hides the stars and causes harm, but it can be fixed fairly easily.
Los Angeles has the worst light pollution in the world.
Birds and humans both need more light at night.
A museum star show is better than watching the real sky.
questions.explain: 文章先說明光害遮住星空並影響鳥類與人類睡眠，再指出光害容易解決並介紹觀星方法，故選 (A)。(B) 文中沒有比較各城市的光害程度；(D) 與文末「沒有什麼比得上真正的夜空」相反。
questions.evidence: The good news is that light pollution is easy to fix

vocab.stem: After years of hard work, she finally ______ her goal of becoming a doctor.
vocab.explain: 經過多年努力，終於「達成」成為醫生的目標，attain a goal 是常見搭配，故選 attained。averted（避開）、audited（查帳；旁聽）、archived（存檔）都不能和「目標」搭配成合理的句子。

vocab.stem: The doctor gave Tom an ______ to treat the infection in his ear.
vocab.explain: 醫生為了治療耳朵的感染而開給 Tom 的是「抗生素」，故選 antibiotic。antonym（反義詞）、archive（檔案）、apprentice（學徒）都不是用來治病的東西。

title: Forests in the Sky
paragraphs: Walk down a busy [[boulevard|L6-0093]] in Milan, Italy, and you may notice two tall apartment towers that look as if a forest has climbed up their sides. Completed in 2014, the Bosco Verticale, or "Vertical Forest," was designed by the architect Stefano Boeri. Its balconies hold hundreds of trees and thousands of smaller plants. Instead of [[beautifying|L6-0080]] the building with paint or glass, Boeri chose to cover it with living green.

The idea is more than decoration. In summer, when the sun [[blazes|L6-0085]] down on the city, the leaves shade the walls and windows and keep the rooms inside cooler, so people need less air conditioning. The plants also catch some of the dust that [[accumulates|L6-0013]] along busy streets, reduce noise, and give birds and insects a place to live high above the ground. Many people complain that tall buildings [[blot|L6-0088]] out the sky; here, people look out at leaves instead. In a crowded city, where every [[acre|L6-0018]] of land is expensive, growing a forest [[upward|L6-0950]] is a clever way to [[broaden|L6-0103]] green space.

Of course, keeping trees alive high above the street is not easy. Strong winds [[batter|L6-0079]] the towers, so the larger trees are tied with steel cables and [[braced|L6-0096]] in their pots. The plants depend on a watering system built into the building, and a [[breakdown|L6-0099]] in that system during a hot summer could quickly harm them. Gardeners, sometimes called "flying gardeners," come down from the roof on ropes to cut branches. Critics also point out a [[blunt|L6-0089]] truth: such buildings cost more to build and to care for, and their apartments are too expensive for most families.

Even so, the [[breadth|L6-0098]] of interest in green architecture keeps growing. Similar towers have since appeared in other cities around the world, and many builders now print [[brochures|L6-0104]] and [[booklets|L6-0091]] showing plants on every floor. A green tower alone cannot solve a city's problems, but it shows that buildings can do more than stand still. With care, they can help nature [[flourish|L6-0352]] in the places where most of us live.
zh: 走在義大利米蘭一條熱鬧的林蔭大道上，你可能會注意到兩棟高聳的公寓大樓，看起來就像有一座森林沿著外牆爬了上去。這座「垂直森林」（Bosco Verticale）於 2014 年完工，由建築師斯特凡諾・博埃里設計。它的陽台上種了數百棵樹和數千株較小的植物。博埃里沒有用油漆或玻璃來美化建築，而是選擇用活生生的綠意把它覆蓋起來。
這個構想不只是裝飾。夏天烈日炙烤城市時，樹葉能遮蔽牆面和窗戶，讓室內保持涼爽，住戶就不必那麼依賴冷氣。植物也能攔下一些沿著繁忙街道累積的灰塵、降低噪音，並讓鳥類和昆蟲在離地很高的地方有個家。許多人抱怨高樓遮蔽了天空；在這裡，人們望出去看到的卻是樹葉。在寸土寸金的擁擠城市裡，讓森林往上生長，是擴大綠地的聰明方法。
當然，要讓樹木在高空中存活並不容易。強風不斷吹打大樓，所以較大的樹會用鋼索綁住，並在盆中加以固定。植物仰賴大樓內建的澆水系統，要是在炎熱的夏天系統故障，植物很快就會受損。園丁有時被稱為「飛天園丁」，他們從屋頂沿著繩索垂降下來修剪樹枝。批評者也直言點出一個事實：這類建築的建造和維護成本較高，裡面的公寓對大多數家庭來說也太貴了。
即便如此，人們對綠色建築的興趣仍不斷擴大。世界其他城市後來也出現了類似的大樓，許多建商現在印製的宣傳手冊和小冊子上，每一層樓都畫著植物。光靠一棟綠色大樓無法解決城市的所有問題，但它證明了建築不只是靜靜地矗立在那裡。只要用心照顧，建築也能幫助大自然在我們大多數人居住的地方欣欣向榮。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what is one benefit of the plants on the towers?
options: They keep the rooms inside cooler in summer.
They make the apartments cheaper to buy.
They stop strong winds from reaching the city.
They grow food for the people living there.
questions.explain: 第二段說夏天時樹葉能遮蔽牆面與窗戶，讓室內保持涼爽，住戶較少需要開冷氣，故選 (A)。(B) 與第三段「公寓對大多數家庭來說太貴」相反。
questions.evidence: keep the rooms inside cooler

questions.stem: Why are the larger trees tied with steel cables?
options: To stop people from cutting them
To keep them in place in strong winds
To carry water to their roots
questions.explain: 第三段說強風吹打大樓，所以較大的樹要用鋼索綁住並固定在盆中，故選 (C)。(D) 植物是靠大樓的澆水系統供水，與鋼索無關。
questions.evidence: Strong winds batter the towers, so the larger trees are tied with steel cables

questions.stem: The word "blunt" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: direct and honest, even if unpleasant
questions.explain: 批評者指出的「事實」是建造成本高、公寓太貴，這是直接而不討喜的實話，故 blunt 在此指「直言不諱的」，選 (B)。(A) 是 blunt 的相反（blunt 原意是「鈍的」）。
questions.evidence: Critics also point out a blunt truth

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the writer's attitude toward vertical forests?
options: The writer thinks they should replace all city parks.
The writer believes they are too dangerous to build.
The writer is mainly worried about their cost to the government.
The writer is hopeful about them but admits they have limits.
questions.explain: 作者介紹了垂直森林的好處，也提到維護困難與成本高等缺點，最後說一棟綠色大樓無法解決城市的所有問題，但仍能幫助大自然繁盛，可見態度樂觀但承認其限制，故選 (D)。(C) 文中提到的是住戶負擔，並未談到政府。
questions.evidence: A green tower alone cannot solve a city's problems

vocab.stem: The two schools signed a ______ agreement to send students to visit each other every summer.
vocab.explain: 兩校互相派學生到對方學校參訪，是「雙邊的」協議，故選 bilateral。bodily（身體的）、blond（金髮的）、bass（低音的）都不能用來形容兩校之間的協議。

vocab.stem: Reading books from different cultures can ______ your view of the world.
vocab.explain: 閱讀不同文化的書可以「拓寬」你的世界觀，broaden one's view 是常見搭配，故選 broaden。bleach（漂白）、batter（猛擊）、boycott（抵制）都不合語意。

title: How Printing Changed the World
paragraphs: Today, a click can send a page to thousands of readers. For most of history, however, every book had to be copied by hand. In [[medieval|L6-0548]] Europe, a monk might spend many months copying a single book, and one [[blot|L6-0088]] of ink could ruin a page he had worked on for days. Books were rare treasures.

Printing actually [[originated|L6-0617]] in East Asia. Chinese printers carved whole pages into blocks of wood. The oldest dated printed book that still exists, a copy of the Diamond Sutra from 868, was found in a cave in Dunhuang and is now kept in the [[archives|L6-0055]] of the British Library. Around the 1040s, a worker named Bi Sheng went further and made separate characters out of clay, which could be arranged into a page and used again. However, because written Chinese uses thousands of characters, this method did not spread widely.

In Europe, the great change came around 1450, when Johannes Gutenberg of Mainz, Germany, built his printing press. Using his skill with metal, Gutenberg made small metal letters. Workers [[aligned|L6-0033]] the letters in neat rows, covered them with ink, and pressed them onto paper. In this way, a press could [[reproduce|L6-0755]] the same page again and again, far faster than any human copier. Setting the letters quickly required real [[proficiency|L6-0700]], and young [[apprentices|L6-0052]] spent years learning the trade. Gutenberg's Bible, finished around 1455, won [[acclaim|L6-0009]] for its beauty.

The effects were enormous. Within a few decades, printing shops had spread to cities across Europe, and books became far cheaper. This new [[abundance|L6-0006]] of books [[broadened|L6-0103]] the group of people who could read and learn. Ideas could now be [[transmitted|L6-0925]] quickly over long distances, and the press [[amplified|L6-0040]] writers' voices. Printers also produced cheap [[booklets|L6-0091]] and news sheets, so ordinary people, not just scholars, could follow the events of their time. As each generation built on the printed work of the last, the [[accumulation|L6-0014]] of knowledge sped up.

Some historians compare the internet to Gutenberg's press. Once again, the [[breadth|L6-0098]] of information available to ordinary people has suddenly grown, and once again, readers must learn to judge what is worth trusting. The tools have changed, but the question is the same: with so much to read, what deserves our attention?
zh: 今天，按一下滑鼠就能把一頁文字傳給成千上萬的讀者。然而在人類歷史的大部分時間裡，每一本書都得靠手抄。在中世紀的歐洲，一位修士可能要花好幾個月才能抄完一本書，而一滴墨漬就可能毀掉他辛苦了好幾天的一頁。書本是稀有的珍寶。
印刷術其實起源於東亞。中國的印刷工把整頁內容刻在木板上。現存最古老、有明確年代的印刷書籍，是一部西元 868 年的《金剛經》，在敦煌的洞窟中被發現，現在收藏在大英圖書館的檔案庫裡。大約在 1040 年代，一位名叫畢昇的工匠更進一步，用黏土做出一個個獨立的字，可以排成一整頁，用完還能重複使用。然而，由於中文書寫需要數千個字，這種方法並沒有廣泛流傳。
在歐洲，重大的轉變發生在 1450 年左右，德國美因茲的約翰尼斯・古騰堡打造了他的印刷機。古騰堡運用他處理金屬的技術，做出小小的金屬字母。工人把字母整齊排成一行行，塗上墨水，再壓印到紙上。如此一來，印刷機就能一次又一次地複製同一頁，速度遠遠超過任何抄寫員。要快速排字需要真正熟練的技術，年輕學徒得花好幾年學習這門手藝。大約在 1455 年完成的古騰堡聖經，因其精美而廣受讚譽。
印刷術的影響非常巨大。短短幾十年內，印刷坊就遍布歐洲各地的城市，書價也大幅下降。書籍變得豐富，讓更多人有機會閱讀和學習。思想如今可以快速傳播到遠方，印刷機也放大了作家的聲音。印刷商還出版便宜的小冊子和新聞單張，讓一般民眾，而不只是學者，也能掌握當時發生的大事。隨著每一代人都在前人印行的成果上繼續發展，知識的累積也加快了腳步。
有些歷史學家把網路比作古騰堡的印刷機。一般人能取得的資訊範圍再次突然擴大，讀者也再次必須學會判斷哪些內容值得信任。工具改變了，但問題依然相同：有這麼多東西可以讀，什麼才值得我們關注？

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The life story of Johannes Gutenberg
Why the internet is better than printed books
How printing developed and changed the way knowledge spread
How monks in medieval Europe copied books
questions.explain: 文章從手抄書談起，介紹東亞的木板印刷與畢昇的活字、古騰堡的印刷機，再說明印刷術如何讓知識廣泛傳播，最後與網路對照，故選 (C)。(A)(D) 都只是文中的一部分內容。
questions.evidence: The effects were enormous.

questions.stem: What is true about Bi Sheng's invention?
options: His clay characters could be used again.
It quickly replaced wooden blocks all over China.
It was made of small metal letters.
It was found in a cave in Dunhuang.
questions.explain: 第二段說畢昇用黏土做出獨立的字，可以排成一頁並重複使用，故選 (A)。(B) 文中說因為中文字數太多，這方法並未廣泛流傳；(C) 金屬字母是古騰堡的做法；(D) 在敦煌發現的是《金剛經》。
questions.evidence: made separate characters out of clay, which could be arranged into a page and used again

questions.stem: Why does the writer mention the internet in the last paragraph?
options: To show that printed books are no longer useful
To explain how the internet was invented
To argue that people should stop reading online
To suggest that people today face a challenge similar to readers after Gutenberg
questions.explain: 最後一段說網路再次讓資訊突然大增，讀者也「再次」必須判斷什麼值得信任，可見作者是在說明今人面對的挑戰與古騰堡時代的讀者相似，故選 (D)。(A)(C) 文中並沒有這樣主張。
questions.evidence: readers must learn to judge what is worth trusting

questions.stem: The word "proficiency" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 要「快速」排字需要 proficiency，後面又說學徒要花好幾年學這門手藝，可知是指「熟練的技術」，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: Setting the letters quickly required real proficiency

vocab.stem: Before the trip, the travel agency mailed us a colorful ______ with maps and hotel information.
vocab.explain: 旅行社寄來一份附有地圖和飯店資訊的彩色「宣傳手冊」，故選 brochure。breakup（分手；解體）、brink（邊緣）、breadth（寬度）都不是可以郵寄、印有資訊的東西。

vocab.stem: The firefighters worked through the night to put out the ______ in the old factory.
vocab.explain: 消防員徹夜工作要撲滅的是「大火」，put out a blaze 是常見搭配，故選 blaze。blot（汙漬）、brace（支架）、breakdown（故障）都不能「撲滅」。

title: Mr. Ho's Only Rule
paragraphs: The summer Pei-shan turned seventeen, she took a job at Ho's Books, a bookstore selling used books on a lane beside a narrow [[brook|L6-0106]]. Business had been slow since a new highway [[bypassed|L6-0111]] the old part of town, and some days only a few customers [[lingered|L6-0510]] among the shelves. Mr. Ho, the owner, did not seem to mind. He refused to [[cater|L6-0128]] to popular taste and still added up prices on an old [[calculator|L6-0113]].

Pei-shan's work was simple. She sat behind the counter as the [[cashier|L6-0125]] and opened [[cardboard|L6-0120]] boxes of donated books. On afternoons when the temperature rose above thirty-five degrees [[Celsius|L6-0133]], the fan did little, and Mr. Ho drank cup after cup of tea, joking that he needed the [[caffeine|L6-0112]] more than the shop needed customers. He had only one [[cardinal|L6-0121]] rule: "Never write in a book." To him, a page with a pen mark was a small [[catastrophe|L6-0127]].

One morning, a delivery driver left a [[bulky|L6-0109]] [[carton|L6-0124]] at the door. Inside were thirty old poetry books, and every one of them broke Mr. Ho's rule. Along the edges of the pages ran notes in beautiful [[calligraphy|L6-0114]]. Some were short, like [[captions|L6-0117]] under photos: "Read by the river, spring 1984." Others described the smell of rain or a song on the radio. The lines [[evoked|L6-0316]] a young reader who had once lived a [[carefree|L6-0122]] life, full of time and feeling.

Pei-shan carried one of the books to the counter, expecting Mr. Ho to frown. Instead, he went quiet. "That's my handwriting," he said. Forty years earlier, as a [[weary|L6-0987]] young teacher who needed money to open the shop, he had sold his own collection to a friend. Now the friend's family had sent the books back.

Mr. Ho cleared a shelf near the window and placed the books there with an [[affectionate|L6-0026]] smile. A small sign beneath them read, "Not for sale." That evening, Pei-shan saw him open the first book and, for the first time in forty years, break his own rule. Under the old note, he wrote one more line: "Home again, summer 2024."
zh: 佩珊十七歲那年夏天，到「何記書店」打工。那是一家賣二手書的書店，位在一條小溪旁的巷子裡。自從新的公路繞過了舊城區，生意就一直很冷清，有些日子只有幾位客人在書架間流連。老闆何先生似乎並不在意。他不肯迎合大眾的口味，結帳時還是用一台舊計算機加總價錢。
佩珊的工作很簡單。她坐在櫃台後面當收銀員，並拆開一箱箱別人捐贈的書。氣溫超過攝氏三十五度的午後，電扇幾乎沒什麼用，何先生一杯接一杯地喝茶，開玩笑說他需要咖啡因的程度，比書店需要客人還多。他只有一條最重要的規矩：「絕對不要在書上寫字。」對他來說，一頁上有筆跡就是一場小災難。
某天早上，送貨司機在門口留下一個笨重的紙箱。裡面是三十本舊詩集，而每一本都違反了何先生的規矩。書頁邊緣寫滿了優美的書法字。有些很短，就像照片下的說明文字：「讀於河邊，1984 年春。」有些則描寫雨的氣味或收音機裡的一首歌。這些字句讓人想起一位曾經無憂無慮、擁有大把時間與豐富情感的年輕讀者。
佩珊拿了一本書到櫃台，以為何先生會皺眉。沒想到他沉默了。「那是我的字。」他說。四十年前，他還是個疲憊的年輕老師，為了籌錢開書店，把自己的藏書賣給了一位朋友。如今，那位朋友的家人把這些書寄了回來。
何先生清出窗邊的一個書架，帶著深情的微笑把書擺上去。書下方的小牌子寫著：「非賣品」。那天傍晚，佩珊看見他翻開第一本書，四十年來第一次打破了自己的規矩。他在舊的筆記下方又寫了一行：「回家了，2024 年夏。」

questions.stem: Why had business at Ho's Books been slow?
options: Mr. Ho refused to sell used books.
The shop was too hot in the summer.
A new highway bypassed the old part of town.
Pei-shan made mistakes as a cashier.
questions.explain: 第一段說自從新的公路繞過舊城區，書店生意就一直很冷清，故選 (C)。(B) 天氣熱是第二段的描述，並不是生意差的原因。
questions.evidence: Business had been slow since a new highway bypassed the old part of town

questions.stem: What was special about the books in the carton?
options: They had notes written along the edges of the pages.
They were written by Pei-shan's teacher.
They had photos with captions inside.
questions.explain: 第三段說每一本書的頁緣都寫滿了優美的書法筆記，違反了何先生的規矩，故選 (A)。(D) 文中是說有些筆記短得「像」照片的說明文字，書裡並沒有照片。
questions.evidence: Along the edges of the pages ran notes in beautiful calligraphy.

questions.stem: The word "cardinal" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 何先生「只有一條」規矩，而且對他來說在書上寫字就是一場小災難，可見這是他「最重要的」規矩，故選 (D)。(A) 是 cardinal 作名詞「紅衣主教；紅雀」的聯想，不合此處語意。
questions.evidence: He had only one cardinal rule

questions.stem: Why did Mr. Ho most likely write in the book at the end of the story?
options: He wanted to make the book easier to sell.
The return of his old books meant so much to him that he wanted to record it.
Pei-shan asked him to write a caption for the sign.
He had forgotten his own rule about books.
questions.explain: 這些書是他四十年前為了開店而賣掉的藏書，如今回到身邊，他深情地把書擺在「非賣品」的書架上，並寫下「回家了」，可見他想記下這份重逢的感動，故選 (B)。(A) 這些書標明不賣。
questions.evidence: Under the old note, he wrote one more line

vocab.stem: This soup is made with chicken ______, carrots, and a little salt.
vocab.explain: 湯的材料包括雞「高湯」、紅蘿蔔和一點鹽，chicken broth 是常見說法，故選 broth。caterpillar（毛毛蟲）、bureaucrat（官僚）、cashier（收銀員）都不是煮湯的材料。

vocab.stem: The museum ______ to young visitors by offering free drawing classes on weekends.
vocab.explain: 博物館週末開設免費繪畫課，是為了「迎合、照顧」年輕參觀者的需求，cater to 是固定用法，故選 caters。broils（烤）、captions（加上說明）、bypasses（繞過）都不能接 to young visitors。

title: Clever in Their Own Ways
paragraphs: For a long time, people believed that using tools was what made humans special. Then, in the 1960s, researchers in Tanzania watched wild [[chimpanzees|L6-0146]] pull the leaves off thin sticks and push the sticks into insect nests to fish out a meal. The discovery [[cemented|L6-0134]] the chimpanzee's place as a skilled tool user, and since then, examples of animal tool use have become almost [[commonplace|L6-0163]] in science. The question is no longer whether animals are clever, but in what ways.

Examples now [[abound|L6-0004]]. Some birds that live by the sea drop [[clams|L6-0151]] onto rocks from the air to break their shells. An octopus in [[captivity|L6-0119]] can learn to open a jar to reach the food inside: it will [[clasp|L6-0152]] the jar with its arms and turn the lid until it comes off. Chimpanzees, meanwhile, form [[coalitions|L6-0158]], with friends supporting one another in disputes over who leads the group.

Some animals even beat us at our own tests. In a well-known study in Japan, a young chimpanzee named Ayumu watched the numbers 1 to 9 appear in different places on a screen. The [[climax|L6-0154]] of the test came when the numbers were shown for less than a second and then covered. Ayumu still touched the hidden places in the right order, doing far better than the university students tested with him.

Animals are also more [[communicative|L6-0165]] than we once thought. One kind of African monkey gives different warning calls for leopards, eagles, and snakes, and the other monkeys react in the right way, such as looking up when they hear the call for an eagle. Dolphins develop their own special whistles, which work a little like names.

In [[colloquial|L6-0161]] English, a foolish person is sometimes called a "birdbrain," but science no longer supports the insult. Each kind of intelligence is an [[adaptation|L6-0019]] to an animal's own life. Perhaps the true sign of a [[civilized|L6-0150]] species is the ability to respect minds very different from its own.
zh: 長久以來，人們認為使用工具是人類與眾不同的地方。後來在 1960 年代，研究人員在坦尚尼亞觀察到野生黑猩猩把細樹枝上的葉子拔掉，再把樹枝伸進昆蟲的巢裡「釣」出食物。這項發現確立了黑猩猩擅長使用工具的地位；從那時起，動物使用工具的例子在科學界幾乎已經司空見慣。問題不再是動物聰不聰明，而是牠們聰明在哪些地方。
如今這樣的例子比比皆是。有些住在海邊的鳥會從空中把蛤蜊丟到岩石上，把殼摔破。圈養的章魚能學會打開罐子，吃到裡面的食物：牠會用觸手緊緊抓住罐子，轉動蓋子直到打開為止。黑猩猩則會結成聯盟，朋友之間在爭奪群體領導地位時互相支持。
有些動物甚至在我們自己設計的測驗中勝過人類。在日本一項著名的研究中，一隻名叫小步（Ayumu）的年輕黑猩猩看著數字 1 到 9 出現在螢幕上的不同位置。測驗的最高潮是數字只顯示不到一秒就被蓋住。小步仍然能依照正確順序點出那些被蓋住的位置，表現遠遠勝過和牠一起受測的大學生。
動物也比我們以前以為的更善於溝通。有一種非洲猴子會針對花豹、老鷹和蛇發出不同的警告叫聲，其他猴子也會做出正確反應，例如聽到代表老鷹的叫聲時就抬頭往上看。海豚會發展出屬於自己的特殊哨音，作用有點像名字。
在英文口語中，愚笨的人有時會被叫作「鳥腦袋」，但科學已經不再支持這種侮辱。每一種智力都是動物為了適應自身生活而發展出來的。或許一個文明物種真正的象徵，是能夠尊重和自己截然不同的心智。

glosses.zh: 笨蛋（字面意思是鳥腦袋）

questions.stem: According to the passage, what do some birds that live by the sea do?
options: They use sticks to fish insects out of nests.
They open jars to reach food.
They give different calls for different enemies.
They drop clams onto rocks to break the shells.
questions.explain: 第二段說有些住在海邊的鳥會從空中把蛤蜊丟到岩石上摔破殼，故選 (D)。(A) 是黑猩猩，(B) 是章魚，(C) 是非洲猴子的行為。
questions.evidence: Some birds that live by the sea drop clams onto rocks from the air to break their shells.

questions.stem: What did Ayumu do in the study in Japan?
options: He taught university students how to count.
He remembered where numbers had been, even after seeing them for less than a second.
He learned to say the numbers 1 to 9.
He used a stick to open a screen.
questions.explain: 第三段說數字只出現不到一秒就被蓋住，小步仍能依正確順序點出那些位置，表現遠勝大學生，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: Ayumu still touched the hidden places in the right order

questions.stem: The word "commonplace" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 自從黑猩猩使用工具的發現之後，動物使用工具的例子越來越多，下一段也說「這樣的例子比比皆是」，可知 commonplace 是「常見的、平凡的」，故選 (C)。(A) 意思正好相反。
questions.evidence: examples of animal tool use have become almost commonplace in science

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Animals show many kinds of intelligence suited to their own lives.
Chimpanzees are smarter than humans in every way.
Only animals that use tools can be called clever.
Scientists should stop testing animals in captivity.
questions.explain: 文章舉出黑猩猩、海鳥、章魚、猴子、海豚等例子，最後說每一種智力都是為了適應動物自身的生活，故選 (A)。(B) 文中只說小步在某項記憶測驗中勝過大學生，並非各方面都比人類聰明。
questions.evidence: Each kind of intelligence is an adaptation to an animal's own life.

vocab.stem: She ______ the old letter tightly in both hands as she read it again.
vocab.explain: 她用雙手「緊握」著那封舊信再讀一遍，故選 clasped。chanted（吟誦）、cloned（複製）、civilized（使開化）都無法和 tightly in both hands 搭配。

vocab.stem: Before the long trip, my grandfather went to the doctor for a ______ to make sure he was healthy.
vocab.explain: 出遠門前去看醫生，確認自己身體健康，是做「健康檢查」，故選 checkup。census（人口普查）、comet（彗星）、clam（蛤蜊）都和看醫生無關。

title: Keep the Letters Coming
paragraphs: To the Editor:

I am writing in response to last week's article about the student council's plan to end our school's pen-pal program with our sister school in Japan. For twelve years, students here have kept up a [[correspondence|L6-0194]] by hand with students there. The council now wants to [[computerize|L6-0173]] the program and replace letters with monthly video calls. I believe this would be a mistake.

The council's main [[contention|L6-0187]] is that letters are slow and old-fashioned, and it [[deems|L6-0225]] them a waste of time. It is true that a letter takes about two weeks to arrive. However, being slow is part of the value. When I write by hand, I cannot simply erase a sentence and type another, and I do not [[abbreviate|L6-0001]] words the way I do in text messages. I have to think before I write, and my letters have become clearer and more [[concise|L6-0176]] as a result.

The article also stated that few students enjoy the program. This [[contradicts|L6-0190]] my own experience. Last month, I [[compiled|L6-0168]] a list of everyone who has joined since the program began, and many of them still write to their pen pals after graduating. When I failed an important exam last winter, one of the first [[consolations|L6-0183]] I received was a card from my pen pal, Haruka. A video call ends when you hang up; a letter can be read again and again.

I am not asking the council to reject every change. As a [[concession|L6-0175]], perhaps we could add one video call each term, so both sides can hear each other's voices. But letters should remain at the heart of the program, for the sake of [[continuity|L6-0189]] with the students who came before us. Ending them suddenly could [[alienate|L6-0032]] the very members the council hopes to serve. Before deciding, the council should carry out a [[comprehensive|L6-0171]] survey of members' views. It will [[convene|L6-0191]] on March 15 to vote, and I encourage anyone who cares about the program to attend. I also thank the [[conscientious|L6-0181]] teachers who have mailed our letters for twelve years.

Sincerely,
Lin Yu-chen, Grade 11
zh: 編輯您好：
我寫這封信，是為了回應上週那篇關於學生會打算終止本校與日本姊妹校筆友計畫的報導。十二年來，我們學校的學生一直用手寫信和那裡的學生通信。學生會現在想把這個計畫電腦化，改用每月一次的視訊通話來取代書信。我認為這會是個錯誤。
學生會的主要論點是書信既慢又過時，並認為寫信是浪費時間。一封信大約要兩週才會寄到，這是事實。然而，慢正是它價值的一部分。當我用手寫信時，我不能隨手擦掉一句話再打上另一句，也不會像傳簡訊那樣把字縮寫。我必須先想清楚再下筆，因此我的信也變得更清楚、更簡潔。
那篇報導也說很少學生喜歡這個計畫。這和我自己的經驗相矛盾。上個月，我彙整了一份計畫開辦以來所有參加者的名單，其中很多人畢業後仍持續寫信給筆友。去年冬天我在一場重要考試中失利時，最先收到的安慰之一，就是筆友春香寄來的卡片。視訊通話掛斷就結束了；一封信卻能讀了又讀。
我並不是要學生會拒絕所有改變。作為讓步，或許我們可以每學期加一次視訊通話，讓雙方能聽聽彼此的聲音。但為了延續與歷屆學長姊之間的傳統，書信應該仍是這個計畫的核心。突然終止寫信，可能會讓學生會原本想服務的成員反而疏遠。在做決定之前，學生會應該針對成員的意見進行全面的調查。學生會將在 3 月 15 日開會表決，我鼓勵所有關心這個計畫的人出席。我也要感謝這十二年來一直盡心盡力幫我們寄信的老師們。

敬上
十一年級　林雨辰

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the letter?
options: To complain about a teacher who mails letters
To ask students to join the student council
To argue that the pen-pal letters should be kept
To explain how to make a video call
questions.explain: 寫信者反對學生會以視訊取代筆友書信，說明寫信的價值、反駁報導內容，並提出折衷方案，目的在主張保留書信，故選 (C)。(A) 寫信者其實是在感謝老師。
questions.evidence: I believe this would be a mistake.

questions.stem: What does the writer suggest as a concession?
options: Ending the program after twelve years
Adding one video call each term
Writing letters only once a year
questions.explain: 第四段說作為讓步，或許可以每學期加一次視訊通話，讓雙方聽聽彼此的聲音，故選 (B)。(A)(D) 都與寫信者希望保留書信的立場相反。
questions.evidence: perhaps we could add one video call each term

questions.stem: According to the writer, how has writing by hand helped her?
options: It has made her handwriting more beautiful.
It has helped her pass an important exam.
It has saved her a lot of time.
It has made her letters clearer and more concise.
questions.explain: 第二段說手寫信必須先想清楚再下筆，因此她的信變得更清楚、更簡潔，故選 (D)。(B) 文中說她其實考試失利了；(C) 寫信者承認書信很慢。
questions.evidence: my letters have become clearer and more concise as a result

questions.stem: In paragraph 4, what does "them" in "Ending them suddenly" refer to?
questions.explain: 前一句說書信應該仍是計畫的核心，接著說突然終止 them 可能讓成員疏遠，可知 them 指的是「書信」，故選 (A)。(B) the members 是被疏遠的對象，不是被終止的東西。
questions.evidence: Ending them suddenly could alienate the very members the council hopes to serve.

vocab.stem: Please keep your summary ______; it should be no longer than fifty words.
vocab.explain: 摘要不能超過五十字，表示要寫得「簡潔」，故選 concise。comprehensive（全面的）意思接近相反；conscientious（盡責的）用來形容人；comparative（比較的）也不合語意。

vocab.stem: The new results ______ what scientists had believed for years, so the textbook had to be changed.
vocab.explain: 新的研究結果「與」科學家多年來的看法「相矛盾」，所以課本必須修改，故選 contradicted。consoled（安慰）、convened（召開）、computerized（電腦化）都無法說明為何課本要改。

title: Alone in a Crowd
paragraphs: It is possible to feel lonely in a [[deafening|L6-0221]] crowd. Many students know the feeling: a cafeteria full of noise, hundreds of friends online, and yet no one to talk to about what really matters. Loneliness is not the same as being alone. Some people enjoy long hours by themselves, while even very [[sociable|L6-0830]] people can feel lonely at a party. What counts is not the number of people around us but whether we feel truly connected to them.

In 2023, the top public health official in the United States released an [[advisory|L6-0024]] describing loneliness as a serious threat to health. Its effects are [[cumulative|L6-0214]]: a few lonely days do little harm, but months or years of feeling cut off can affect sleep, mood, and even the heart.

Why does modern life leave some people feeling so alone? One reason may be that screens have become our [[default|L6-0226]] way of keeping in touch. Social media can [[dazzle|L6-0220]] us with photos of other people's exciting lives, leaving us feeling left out. For some, the phone becomes a [[crutch|L6-0210]]: it may [[soothe|L6-0839]] us for a moment, but it does not meet the deeper need for real conversation. Others become [[cynical|L6-0219]] and decide that friendship is simply not worth the effort.

Fortunately, friendships can be [[cultivated|L6-0213]], much like a garden, and doing so takes [[dedication|L6-0223]] rather than luck. Small steps can help [[curb|L6-0215]] loneliness: invite a classmate for a walk, join a club, or put your phone away at dinner. Some neighborhoods turn an empty [[courtyard|L6-0199]] into a shared garden or set up a [[cozy|L6-0201]] reading corner where neighbors can meet. A [[cosmetic|L6-0195]] change like brighter paint will not solve the problem, but spaces that bring people together can.

If you feel lonely, it does not mean something is wrong with you. Like hunger, loneliness is a signal that you need something. Taking one [[decisive|L6-0222]] step, such as messaging an old friend or saying yes to an invitation, can be the start of a change. And if a classmate is sitting alone, you could be the one who says hello.
zh: 在震耳欲聾的人群中也可能感到孤單。許多學生都懂這種感覺：餐廳裡人聲鼎沸，網路上有好幾百個朋友，卻沒有一個人能聊聊真正重要的事。孤獨感和獨處並不相同。有些人很享受長時間獨處，而即使是很愛交際的人，也可能在派對上感到寂寞。重要的不是身邊有多少人，而是我們是否真的覺得和他們有所連結。
2023 年，美國最高公共衛生官員發布了一份公告，將孤獨感描述為對健康的嚴重威脅。它的影響是逐漸累積的：寂寞個幾天不會造成太大傷害，但如果好幾個月甚至好幾年都覺得與人隔絕，就可能影響睡眠、情緒，甚至心臟。
為什麼現代生活讓有些人感到如此孤單？原因之一可能是螢幕已經成為我們保持聯絡的預設方式。社群媒體上別人精彩生活的照片讓我們眼花撩亂，也讓我們覺得自己被排除在外。對有些人來說，手機變成了一根拐杖：它或許能暫時安撫我們，卻無法滿足我們對真正對話的深層需求。另一些人則變得憤世嫉俗，認定友誼根本不值得付出心力。
幸好，友誼就像花園一樣可以培養，而這需要的是用心投入，而非運氣。一些小步驟就能幫助減輕孤獨感：約同學一起散步、參加社團，或在吃晚餐時把手機收起來。有些社區把空蕩蕩的中庭改造成共享花園，或布置一個溫馨的閱讀角落，讓鄰居有地方相聚。像把牆漆得更亮這種表面上的改變無法解決問題，但能把人們聚在一起的空間可以。
如果你感到寂寞，並不代表你有什麼問題。就像飢餓一樣，孤獨感是一個訊號，提醒你需要某些東西。踏出果斷的一步，例如傳訊息給老朋友，或答應一次邀約，就可能是改變的開始。如果你看到有同學獨自坐著，你也可以成為那個先打招呼的人。

questions.stem: According to the passage, which statement about loneliness is true?
options: It only happens to people who are not sociable.
It is different from simply being alone.
It always disappears after a few days.
It cannot be changed once it starts.
questions.explain: 第一段說孤獨感和獨處並不相同，即使很愛交際的人也可能感到寂寞，故選 (B)。(A) 與「連很愛交際的人也會寂寞」相反；(D) 與第四、五段提出的改善方法相反。
questions.evidence: Loneliness is not the same as being alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is mentioned as a way to help curb loneliness?
options: Spending more time on social media
Painting your room a brighter color
Waiting for others to send you messages
Inviting a classmate for a walk
questions.explain: 第四段列出減輕孤獨感的小步驟：約同學散步、參加社團、吃晚餐時把手機收起來，故選 (D)。(B) 文中說這種表面的改變無法解決問題；(A) 社群媒體反而可能讓人覺得被排除在外。
questions.evidence: invite a classmate for a walk

questions.stem: The word "cumulative" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: growing stronger as it builds up over time
questions.explain: 冒號後解釋：寂寞幾天傷害不大，但好幾個月或好幾年就可能影響健康，可知 cumulative 是「逐漸累積的」，故選 (A)。(B) 與文意相反。
questions.evidence: Its effects are cumulative

questions.stem: What does the writer suggest about phones?
options: They are the main reason people join clubs.
They should be banned in schools.
They can bring short-term comfort but cannot replace real conversation.
They help cynical people make new friends.
questions.explain: 第三段說手機像拐杖，或許能暫時安撫我們，卻無法滿足對真正對話的深層需求，故選 (C)。(B) 作者只建議吃晚餐時收起手機，並沒有主張禁止。
questions.evidence: it may soothe us for a moment, but it does not meet the deeper need for real conversation

vocab.stem: After the long hike, Amy got a painful ______ in her leg and had to stop.
vocab.explain: 長途健行後腿部出現疼痛、不得不停下來，是「抽筋」，故選 cramp。coupon（折價券）、curfew（宵禁）、crater（火山口）都不會長在腿上。

vocab.stem: With a ______ for twenty percent off, Jenny bought the shoes for much less.
vocab.explain: 有一張打八折的「折價券」，所以 Jenny 買鞋省了不少錢，故選 coupon。crutch（拐杖）、courtyard（庭院）、crocodile（鱷魚）都不能讓人打折。

title: Why Forgetting Is Not Failing
paragraphs: In the 1880s, the German scientist Hermann Ebbinghaus carried out a strange experiment on himself. He memorized long lists of nonsense syllables such as "WID" and "ZOF," which had no meaning he could connect to anything he already knew. He then tested himself at different times. To his [[disbelief|L6-0253]], a large part of what he had learned was gone within a day. The pattern he found became known as the "forgetting curve": memory drops quickly at first and then more slowly.

To many students, this sounds like bad news. If we forget so fast, are our exam hopes [[destined|L6-0235]] to fail? Not necessarily. Ebbinghaus also found that each time he reviewed a list, he forgot it more slowly. This is why spreading review over several days works better than [[cramming|L6-0204]] everything the night before. Students who [[devour|L6-0241]] a whole textbook in one night may feel ready, but much of it will soon be gone.

Sleep plays a key role, too. While we sleep, the brain appears to review and strengthen the day's memories. Students who are [[deprived|L6-0232]] of sleep before a test may find that facts they studied simply will not come back. Staying up all night [[depletes|L6-0231]] the energy the brain needs, and the results can be [[disastrous|L6-0252]].

Even more surprising, many scientists now believe that forgetting is not simply a failure of memory. If we remembered every detail of every day, it would be hard to [[differentiate|L6-0248]] between what matters and what does not. By letting less important details fade, the brain keeps the important patterns clear, and the memories we use often [[linger|L6-0510]] for years. Researchers have not yet found a [[definitive|L6-0229]] answer about how this works, but a healthy memory seems to need both remembering and forgetting.

For learners, the lesson is practical. Do not let the forgetting curve [[deter|L6-0239]] you; plan for it. [[Rehearse|L6-0744]] new words a day after learning them and again a few days later, test yourself instead of just reading your notes again, and protect your sleep. Even an old-fashioned [[dictation|L6-0244]] quiz helps, because pulling words out of memory makes them last.
zh: 1880 年代，德國科學家赫曼・艾賓豪斯在自己身上做了一項奇特的實驗。他背下一長串無意義的音節，例如「WID」和「ZOF」，這些音節和他已知的任何事物都連不上關係。接著他在不同的時間點測驗自己。令他難以置信的是，學過的內容有一大部分在一天之內就忘掉了。他發現的這個模式後來被稱為「遺忘曲線」：記憶一開始下降得很快，之後才慢慢趨緩。
對許多學生來說，這聽起來像是壞消息。如果我們忘得這麼快，考試的希望豈不是注定落空？其實不見得。艾賓豪斯也發現，每複習一次清單，他遺忘的速度就變得更慢。這就是為什麼把複習分散到好幾天，效果會比考前一晚臨時抱佛腳更好。一個晚上狼吞虎嚥地讀完整本課本的學生，也許會覺得準備好了，但大部分內容很快就會忘光。
睡眠也扮演關鍵角色。我們睡覺時，大腦似乎會複習並強化白天的記憶。考前睡眠不足的學生，可能會發現讀過的內容就是想不起來。熬夜會耗盡大腦需要的能量，結果可能非常慘。
更令人驚訝的是，現在許多科學家認為，遺忘不只是記憶的失敗。如果我們記得每一天的每一個細節，就很難分辨什麼重要、什麼不重要。藉由讓較不重要的細節淡去，大腦能讓重要的模式保持清晰，而我們經常使用的記憶則能保留好幾年。研究人員對這個機制還沒有找到確切的答案，但健康的記憶似乎同時需要記住與遺忘。
對學習者來說，這個道理很實用。別讓遺忘曲線嚇退你；要事先為它做好準備。新單字學完後隔一天複習一次，過幾天再複習一次；用自我測驗取代單純重讀筆記；並且保護好你的睡眠。就連老派的聽寫小考也有幫助，因為把單字從記憶中提取出來，正是讓它們記得更久的關鍵。

questions.stem: What did Ebbinghaus memorize in his experiment?
questions.explain: 第一段說艾賓豪斯背下一長串無意義的音節，例如 WID 和 ZOF，故選 (C)。這些音節故意選成與已知事物無關，因此 (A)(D) 都不對。
questions.evidence: He memorized long lists of nonsense syllables

questions.stem: According to the passage, what happened each time Ebbinghaus reviewed a list?
options: He could no longer remember it at all.
questions.explain: 第二段說艾賓豪斯發現每複習一次清單，遺忘的速度就變得更慢，故選 (A)。(B) 與文意相反。
questions.evidence: each time he reviewed a list, he forgot it more slowly

questions.stem: The phrase "deprived of" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 後文說這些學生會想不起讀過的內容，並提到熬夜的後果，可知 deprived of sleep 是「被剝奪睡眠、睡不夠」，故選 (D)。(B) 意思正好相反。
questions.evidence: Students who are deprived of sleep before a test

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Students should study all night before an exam.
Forgetting is natural and even useful, and learners can plan for it.
Ebbinghaus proved that memory never fades.
Dictation is the only good way to learn new words.
questions.explain: 文章介紹遺忘曲線，說明遺忘其實有助大腦分辨重要的事，並建議分散複習、自我測驗和保護睡眠，故選 (B)。(A) 與文中「熬夜結果可能很慘」相反；(D) 聽寫只是例子之一。
questions.evidence: a healthy memory seems to need both remembering and forgetting

vocab.stem: We use this ______ to wash our clothes; it removes even oily stains.
vocab.explain: 用來洗衣服、連油漬都能去除的是「清潔劑」，故選 detergent。diesel（柴油）、descent（下降；血統）、diabetes（糖尿病）都不能拿來洗衣服。

vocab.stem: The heavy rain did not ______ thousands of fans from coming to the concert.
vocab.explain: 大雨並沒有「阻止」數千名歌迷前來聽演唱會，deter sb. from V-ing 是固定用法，故選 deter。deplete（耗盡）、dictate（口述；支配）、devour（吞食）都不能接 from coming。

title: The Silent Army Under the Fields
paragraphs: In March 1974, a group of farmers near the city of Xi'an, China, were digging a well in a field they had [[cultivated|L6-0213]] for years. A few meters down, their tools hit something hard: pieces of baked clay shaped like parts of a human body. When experts arrived, they could only stare in [[disbelief|L6-0253]]. Buried beneath the fields was an army of life-sized [[ceramic|L6-0136]] soldiers, one of the greatest finds in the history of [[archaeology|L6-0054]].

The soldiers had been made to guard the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, the ruler who united China in 221 BC and became its first emperor. During his [[reign|L6-0745]], he [[dictated|L6-0243]] everything from weights and measures to the way characters were written. Believing he was [[destined|L6-0235]] to rule even after death, he began preparing his tomb long before he died in 210 BC.

Since then, experts have [[compiled|L6-0168]] a [[comprehensive|L6-0171]] record of the site. Three main pits have been explored, and they hold thousands of soldiers, along with horses and carriages. Most figures were found broken, and workers have shown great [[dedication|L6-0223]], fitting them back together piece by piece. Although the bodies were made from a limited number of basic forms, the faces, hair, and clothing vary so much that it is hard to find two exactly alike. Differences in height and dress help experts [[differentiate|L6-0248]] generals from ordinary soldiers.

Today the figures look gray and brown, but they were once painted in bright colors. Sadly, when the soldiers meet the dry air, much of the paint can curl and [[detach|L6-0236]] from the clay within minutes. For researchers, losing these colors was a small [[catastrophe|L6-0127]]. For this reason, digging has moved slowly, and scientists keep searching for better ways to protect what remains. In the museum, short [[captions|L6-0117]] beside the figures explain what each soldier once looked like.

The emperor's own tomb, under a large hill nearby, has never been opened. An ancient historian wrote that it held rivers of mercury, and modern tests of the soil there have found very high levels of this metal. Until there is a [[definitive|L6-0229]] way to protect what lies inside, experts have chosen to wait. Meanwhile, the silent army, added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1987, continues to amaze visitors from around the world.
zh: 1974 年 3 月，中國西安附近的一群農民正在他們耕種多年的田裡挖井。挖到幾公尺深時，他們的工具碰到了某個堅硬的東西：一些形狀像人體部位的燒製陶土碎片。專家趕到時，也只能難以置信地瞪大眼睛。田地底下埋著一支與真人一樣大小的陶製士兵大軍，這是考古史上最重大的發現之一。
這些士兵是為了守衛秦始皇的陵墓而製作的。秦始皇在西元前 221 年統一中國，成為中國第一位皇帝。在位期間，他規定了從度量衡到文字寫法的一切。他相信自己注定在死後仍要繼續統治，因此早在西元前 210 年去世之前很久，就開始籌建自己的陵墓。
從那時起，專家們為這處遺址彙整了一份全面的紀錄。目前已經發掘了三座主要的坑，裡面有數千名士兵，還有馬匹和車。大部分陶俑出土時都已破碎，工作人員展現了極大的投入，一塊一塊地把它們拼回原狀。雖然陶俑的身體是用有限的幾種基本形式製作的，但臉部、髮型和服裝變化多端，很難找到兩個完全相同的。身高和服裝的差異能幫助專家區分將軍與一般士兵。
今天這些陶俑看起來是灰褐色的，但它們原本漆著鮮豔的色彩。可惜的是，陶俑一接觸到乾燥的空氣，許多顏料在幾分鐘內就會捲起並從陶土上剝落。對研究人員來說，失去這些色彩是一場小小的災難。因此，挖掘工作進行得很緩慢，科學家也持續尋找更好的方法來保護殘存的部分。在博物館裡，陶俑旁的簡短說明會解釋每位士兵原本的模樣。
皇帝本人的陵墓位在附近的一座大土丘下，至今從未被打開。一位古代歷史學家寫道，陵墓裡有水銀流成的河，而現代對當地土壤的檢測也發現這種金屬的含量非常高。在找到確切可行的方法來保護裡面的東西之前，專家們選擇等待。與此同時，這支沉默的大軍在 1987 年被列入聯合國教科文組織的世界遺產名錄，持續讓來自世界各地的遊客驚嘆不已。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How farmers in China grow their crops
The life and wars of China's first emperor
Why the colors of ancient paintings fade
The discovery of a clay army and what experts have learned about it
questions.explain: 文章從農民挖井發現陶俑談起，介紹陶俑的由來、發掘與修復、色彩保存問題，以及尚未開啟的皇帝陵墓，故選 (D)。(B) 秦始皇只是第二段的背景介紹。
questions.evidence: Buried beneath the fields was an army of life-sized ceramic soldiers

questions.stem: How was the clay army first discovered?
options: Experts found it while studying an ancient book.
Farmers digging a well found pieces of baked clay.
Workers building a museum hit a clay soldier.
A historian described where it was buried.
questions.explain: 第一段說 1974 年農民在田裡挖井時，工具碰到了形狀像人體部位的陶土碎片，故選 (B)。(D) 古代歷史學家記載的是皇帝陵墓裡的水銀河，並非陶俑的位置。
questions.evidence: a group of farmers near the city of Xi'an, China, were digging a well

questions.stem: Why have experts most likely not opened the emperor's own tomb?
options: They are afraid of damaging what is inside before they have a safe method.
They believe the tomb is empty.
The government has sold the land to farmers.
Visitors have asked them to keep it closed.
questions.explain: 第五段說在找到確切可行的保護方法之前，專家選擇等待；第四段也提到陶俑上的顏料一接觸空氣就剝落，可推知他們擔心開啟後會損壞文物，故選 (A)。
questions.evidence: Until there is a definitive way to protect what lies inside, experts have chosen to wait.

questions.stem: The word "detach" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 顏料一接觸乾燥空氣就會捲起並 detach from the clay，導致陶俑失去色彩，可知 detach 是「脫落、分離」，故選 (C)。(A) 與色彩消失的文意相反。
questions.evidence: much of the paint can curl and detach from the clay within minutes

vocab.stem: Many people stared in ______ when the small team beat the world champions.
vocab.explain: 小球隊擊敗世界冠軍，令許多人「難以置信」地瞪大眼睛，stare in disbelief 是常見搭配，故選 disbelief。descent（下降）、diplomacy（外交）、detention（拘留；課後留校）都不合語意。

vocab.stem: Eating too much sugar for many years can raise your risk of ______.
vocab.explain: 長年吃太多糖會增加罹患「糖尿病」的風險，故選 diabetes。diesel（柴油）、dictation（聽寫）、directive（指令）都不是疾病。

title: The Price of a Song
paragraphs: Lying in her [[dormitory|L6-0277]] room, a college student can [[doze|L6-0280]] off to fifty songs without paying for a single one directly. For listeners, streaming has been a gift: a huge library of music for a monthly fee, or even for free with advertisements. Many of us are so [[accustomed|L6-0016]] to it that buying a song seems strange. For musicians, however, the picture is more complicated.

Streaming services do not sell songs one at a time. Instead, they collect money from monthly fees and advertising, and payments are then [[computed|L6-0172]] mainly according to how often each song is played. The amount for a single play is tiny, usually less than one cent, and it is shared among record companies, song writers, and performers. Many musicians reacted with [[dismay|L6-0262]] when they saw how little they earned, and some called for fuller [[disclosure|L6-0258]] of how the money is divided. Some even warned that the system would [[doom|L6-0276]] small, independent artists.

Others see things differently. Before streaming, many people simply copied music online without paying at all. Streaming offered an easy, legal choice, and money began flowing back into the music business. There is [[dissent|L6-0268]] even among artists. Some say streaming helps new singers find fans around the world, while others fear that the [[abundance|L6-0006]] of choice makes music feel [[disposable|L6-0265]], something to skip after ten seconds.

To survive, many musicians now [[diversify|L6-0272]] their income. Concerts, T-shirts, and fan events have become more important, and some artists try to [[divert|L6-0274]] fans' attention from free streams toward concert tickets or vinyl records. Others play a [[dual|L6-0285]] role, writing songs for other singers while also performing their own. For many, building a loyal group of fans slowly pays [[dividends|L6-0275]] that streaming numbers alone cannot show.

When millions of songs are just one tap away, any single song may seem [[dispensable|L6-0263]]. Yet someone wrote it, practiced it, and recorded it. The claim that one listener can save the music business may be [[dubious|L6-0286]], but buying a concert ticket or telling a friend about a song you love is a small way of showing that music matters.
zh: 躺在宿舍房間裡，一位大學生可以聽著五十首歌打瞌睡，卻沒有直接為任何一首付錢。對聽眾來說，串流音樂是一份大禮：每月付一筆費用，甚至靠廣告就能免費享用龐大的音樂庫。我們許多人早已習慣這種方式，以至於買一首歌反而顯得奇怪。然而對音樂人來說，情況就複雜多了。
串流服務並不是一首一首地賣歌。它們從月費和廣告收取收入，再主要依照每首歌被播放的次數來計算款項。一次播放的金額非常少，通常不到一美分，而且還要由唱片公司、詞曲作者和演出者分享。許多音樂人看到自己賺得這麼少時都感到很沮喪，有些人呼籲更完整地公開金錢分配的方式。有些人甚至警告，這套制度會讓小型獨立音樂人注定失敗。
也有人持不同看法。在串流出現之前，許多人乾脆在網路上複製音樂，完全不付錢。串流提供了一個簡單又合法的選擇，資金也開始回流到音樂產業。即使在音樂人之間也存在歧見。有些人說串流幫助新歌手在世界各地找到歌迷，另一些人則擔心選擇太多，讓音樂顯得用完即丟，聽十秒就跳過。
為了生存，許多音樂人現在讓收入來源多樣化。演唱會、T 恤和歌迷活動變得更加重要，有些藝人會設法把歌迷的注意力從免費串流轉移到演唱會門票或黑膠唱片上。也有人身兼雙重角色，一邊為其他歌手寫歌，一邊演唱自己的作品。對許多人來說，慢慢累積一群忠實歌迷所帶來的回報，是串流數字本身看不出來的。
當數百萬首歌只要輕觸一下就能聽到，任何一首歌似乎都可有可無。然而，總有人寫下它、練習它、錄製它。說一位聽眾就能拯救音樂產業，這種說法也許令人存疑，但買一張演唱會門票，或是把你喜愛的歌告訴朋友，都是表示音樂很重要的小小方式。

questions.stem: According to the passage, how are streaming payments mainly decided?
options: By how many albums an artist has sold
By how famous each singer is
By how often each song is played
By how long each song is
questions.explain: 第二段說串流服務主要依照每首歌被播放的次數來計算款項，故選 (C)。(A) 串流服務並不是一首一首地賣歌，也不看專輯銷量。
questions.evidence: payments are then computed mainly according to how often each song is played

questions.stem: What do some artists do to earn more money?
options: Encourage fans to buy concert tickets or vinyl records
Ask streaming services to stop playing their songs
Give their concert tickets away for free
Stop writing songs for other singers
questions.explain: 第四段說有些藝人設法把歌迷的注意力從免費串流轉移到演唱會門票或黑膠唱片上，故選 (A)。(D) 與文中「有人一邊替別的歌手寫歌一邊演唱自己作品」相反。
questions.evidence: some artists try to divert fans' attention from free streams toward concert tickets or vinyl records

questions.stem: The word "dissent" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 後文說有些音樂人認為串流幫助新歌手，另一些人卻擔心串流讓音樂變得用完即丟，可見意見不一致，dissent 是「歧見、不同意」，故選 (B)。
questions.evidence: There is dissent even among artists.

questions.stem: What does the writer suggest at the end of the passage?
options: Listeners should stop using streaming services.
One listener can save the whole music business.
Most songs are not worth listening to.
Listeners can show they value music through small actions.
questions.explain: 最後一段說一位聽眾能拯救音樂產業的說法令人存疑，但買演唱會門票或向朋友推薦歌曲，都是表示音樂很重要的小方式，故選 (D)。(B) 正是作者認為令人存疑的說法。
questions.evidence: is a small way of showing that music matters

vocab.stem: Please throw these ______ cups into the recycling bin after the party.
vocab.explain: 派對後要丟進回收桶的是「免洗、用完即丟的」杯子，故選 disposable。discreet（謹慎的）、dubious（可疑的）、disciplinary（紀律的）都不能用來形容紙杯。

vocab.stem: The nurse will ______ the medicine to patients at eight o'clock every morning.
vocab.explain: 護理師每天早上八點把藥「分發」給病人，dispense medicine 是常見搭配，故選 dispense。doze（打瞌睡）是不及物動詞，diversify（使多樣化）、doom（注定失敗）都不合語意。

title: Ancient Eyes on the Sky
paragraphs: Long before the first telescope, people stood outside at [[dusk|L6-0288]] and watched the sky slowly fill with stars. Many believed the heavens were the [[dwelling|L6-0291]] of gods, and the stars, which seemed to stay in the same places for [[eternity|L6-0313]], looked like messages from those gods. People who could read these messages were held in high [[esteem|L6-0312]]. Farmers asked them when to plant, and sailors learned from them how to [[navigate|L6-0586]] at night.

Some of the most careful early records come from Babylon, in what is now Iraq. For hundreds of years, Babylonian sky-watchers wrote down what they saw on clay tablets. Spending night after night outdoors, some of them may have seemed [[eccentric|L6-0292]] to their neighbors, but their [[endeavor|L6-0302]] paid off. By comparing records that [[spanned|L6-0843]] many generations, they found that [[eclipses|L6-0293]] of the moon followed a pattern, and they learned to predict when the next one might come.

Eclipses frightened many ancient peoples. In China, a popular story said that a hungry dog in the heavens was trying to eat the sun, so people beat drums to scare it away. Many cultures [[equated|L6-0310]] a dark sun with bad news for the ruler. Today we know why a total eclipse of the sun is possible at all. The sun is about 400 times wider than the moon and completely [[dwarfs|L6-0289]] it, but it is also about 400 times farther away. That is why the two look almost the same size in the sky, and why the moon can cover the sun so perfectly.

The Greeks used eclipses to learn about Earth itself. During an eclipse of the moon, Aristotle noticed that Earth's shadow on the moon was always curved, and he [[inferred|L6-0448]] that Earth must be round. Later, Ptolemy collected Greek knowledge of the sky in one great book. It worked almost like an [[encyclopedia|L6-0301]] of [[astronomy|L6-0064]] and was used for more than a thousand years. These early thinkers [[elevated|L6-0297]] sky-watching from simple stories to a true science, and their patient work still [[enlightens|L6-0306]] us today.
zh: 早在第一架望遠鏡出現之前，人們就會在黃昏時站在戶外，看著天空慢慢布滿星星。許多人相信天上是眾神的住所，而那些彷彿永遠停在原處的星星，就像是眾神傳來的訊息。能解讀這些訊息的人備受尊敬。農夫向他們請教何時播種，水手則跟他們學習如何在夜間航行。
早期最細心的一些紀錄來自巴比倫，也就是今天的伊拉克一帶。幾百年來，巴比倫的觀星者把看到的天象寫在泥板上。他們一夜又一夜待在戶外，在鄰居眼中或許有些古怪，但他們的努力有了回報。比較了跨越好幾個世代的紀錄之後，他們發現月蝕有一定的規律，並學會預測下一次月蝕可能何時發生。
日月蝕讓許多古代民族感到害怕。在中國，一個流傳很廣的說法是天上有一隻餓狗想把太陽吃掉，所以人們敲鑼打鼓要把牠嚇跑。許多文化都把太陽變暗和統治者將遇到壞事畫上等號。今天我們知道日全蝕為什麼有可能發生。太陽的寬度大約是月亮的 400 倍，讓月亮顯得渺小，但太陽離我們的距離也大約是月亮的 400 倍遠。因此兩者在天空中看起來幾乎一樣大，月亮也才能把太陽遮得剛剛好。
希臘人則利用日月蝕來認識地球本身。亞里斯多德注意到，月蝕時地球投在月亮上的影子總是彎曲的，因而推論地球一定是圓的。後來，托勒密把希臘人對天空的知識收錄在一部巨著裡。這本書幾乎就像一部天文學百科全書，被使用了一千多年。這些早期的思想家把觀星從單純的故事提升為真正的科學，他們耐心的研究至今仍啟發著我們。

questions.stem: What did the Babylonian sky-watchers learn from their records?
options: They proved that Earth is round.
They could predict eclipses of the moon.
They measured the exact size of the sun.
questions.explain: 第二段說巴比倫觀星者比較跨越好幾個世代的紀錄，發現月蝕有規律，並學會預測下一次月蝕，故選 (B)。(A) 推論地球是圓的是希臘的亞里斯多德。
questions.evidence: they found that eclipses of the moon followed a pattern, and they learned to predict when the next one might come

questions.stem: According to the passage, why can the moon cover the sun so perfectly during a total eclipse?
options: The moon becomes larger during an eclipse.
The sun becomes smaller during an eclipse.
The sun is about 400 times wider than the moon but also about 400 times farther away.
The moon and the sun are exactly the same size.
questions.explain: 第三段說太陽寬度約為月亮的 400 倍，但距離也約遠 400 倍，所以兩者看起來幾乎一樣大，月亮才能剛好遮住太陽，故選 (C)。(D) 與「太陽寬約 400 倍」的說法相反。
questions.evidence: but it is also about 400 times farther away

questions.stem: The word "dwarfs" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: makes something look small by comparison
questions.explain: 太陽比月亮寬約 400 倍，兩相比較之下月亮顯得很小，所以 dwarfs 在此指「使相形見絀、使顯得渺小」，故選 (A)。(B)「遮住」是月亮對太陽做的事，方向剛好相反。
questions.evidence: The sun is about 400 times wider than the moon and completely dwarfs it

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why eclipses frightened people in ancient China
The life and ideas of Aristotle
How to watch an eclipse safely
How ancient peoples studied the sky and what they learned
questions.explain: 全文介紹古人觀星的動機、巴比倫的紀錄、對日月蝕的看法，以及希臘人如何由此認識地球，最後說他們把觀星提升為科學，故選 (D)。(A)、(B) 都只是其中一段的內容。
questions.evidence: These early thinkers elevated sky-watching from simple stories to a true science

vocab.stem: When the river rose quickly after the storm, the police had to ______ hundreds of families from their homes.
vocab.explain: 河水在暴風雨後快速上漲，警方必須把數百戶人家從家中「撤離」，故選 evacuate。equalize（使相等）、enroll（使註冊）、elevate（提升）都不能接 from their homes 表示帶離危險地區。

vocab.stem: Before the speaking test began, the ______ explained the rules and smiled to help the students relax.
vocab.explain: 口試開始前說明規則、讓考生放鬆的人是「主考官」，故選 examiner。emigrant（移民）、electrician（電工）與口試無關，encyclopedia（百科全書）不會說明規則或微笑。

title: Life Where Rain Rarely Falls
paragraphs: To many people, a desert looks empty: sand as far as the eye can see, little rain, and a sun so strong that the ground can feel like an oven. In some deserts, summer temperatures can rise above 120 degrees [[Fahrenheit|L6-0335]]. A [[feeble|L6-0340]] plant or animal would not last long here. Yet life [[abounds|L6-0004]] in deserts, and the creatures that [[dwell|L6-0290]] there [[excel|L6-0319]] at one difficult task: staying alive with very little water.

Take the camel. Many people believe that its back stores water, but this is a [[fable|L6-0333]]; the large lump on its back actually stores fat. A camel's real strength is how well it protects itself. Two rows of long [[eyelashes|L6-0330]] keep sand away from its eyes, and a thin third [[eyelid|L6-0331]] can wipe the eyes clean, so the animal does not damage its [[eyesight|L6-0332]] when strong winds blow sand around. It can even close its nose to keep the sand out.

Smaller animals have their own tricks. The fennec fox, the smallest fox in the world, has huge ears that help it get rid of [[excess|L6-0321]] body heat. The kangaroo rat may go its whole life without drinking. Instead, its body is able to [[extract|L6-0328]] enough water from the dry seeds it eats. Most desert animals also avoid [[exerting|L6-0324]] themselves in the heat of the day. They rest in holes in the ground and come out at night, which reduces their [[expenditure|L6-0325]] of energy and water.

Plants, too, must not [[falter|L6-0336]] in this harsh place. A cactus [[conserves|L6-0182]] water inside its thick stem, and its sharp spines, which take the place of leaves, lose far less water than leaves would. Many desert seeds wait in the ground for years. When a rare heavy rain finally comes, they grow, flower, and drop new seeds within a few weeks, before the water disappears.

Deserts are not the empty places they seem. For anyone with a [[fascination|L6-0338]] with nature, they are full of surprises. The more [[familiarity|L6-0337]] we gain with these clever survivors, the more we can learn about using water wisely ourselves.
zh: 在許多人眼中，沙漠看起來空無一物：放眼望去全是沙子，雨水稀少，陽光強烈到地面摸起來像烤箱一樣燙。有些沙漠的夏季氣溫可以超過華氏 120 度。虛弱的植物或動物在這裡撐不了多久。然而沙漠裡其實充滿生命，住在那裡的生物都非常擅長一件困難的事：靠著極少的水活下去。
以駱駝為例。許多人以為駱駝的背儲存著水，但這只是一個流傳的說法；牠背上的大隆起其實儲存的是脂肪。駱駝真正厲害的地方，在於牠保護自己的能力。兩排長長的睫毛能擋住沙子，不讓沙子跑進眼睛，薄薄的第三層眼皮還能把眼睛擦乾淨，所以強風吹起沙子時，牠的視力也不會受損。牠甚至可以把鼻子閉起來，不讓沙子進去。
體型較小的動物也有自己的妙招。耳廓狐是世界上最小的狐狸，牠的大耳朵能幫助散去身體多餘的熱。更格盧鼠（袋鼠鼠）可能一輩子都不喝水，牠的身體能從所吃的乾種子中取得足夠的水分。大多數沙漠動物也會避免在白天最熱的時候耗費體力。牠們躲在地洞裡休息，晚上才出來活動，藉此減少能量與水分的消耗。
植物在這個嚴酷的環境中也不能有絲毫鬆懈。仙人掌把水保存在粗厚的莖裡，而取代葉子的尖刺所散失的水分比葉子少得多。許多沙漠植物的種子會在土裡等上好幾年。等到難得的大雨終於降下，它們會在短短幾週內發芽、開花並結出新的種子，趕在水分消失之前完成。
沙漠並不是看起來那樣空無一物的地方。對任何著迷於大自然的人來說，沙漠充滿了驚喜。我們對這些聰明的生存高手越熟悉，就越能學到如何聰明地用水。

questions.stem: What does the large lump on a camel's back actually store?
questions.explain: 第二段說許多人以為駱駝背上存的是水，但那只是誤傳，其實儲存的是脂肪，故選 (D)。(A) 正是文中說的錯誤觀念。
questions.evidence: the large lump on its back actually stores fat

questions.stem: How does the kangaroo rat get the water it needs?
options: Its body gets water from the dry seeds it eats.
It stores water in its huge ears.
It drinks from pools after a rare rain.
It drinks the water stored inside cactus stems.
questions.explain: 第三段說更格盧鼠可能一輩子不喝水，而是由身體從吃下的乾種子中取得足夠水分，故選 (A)。(B) 大耳朵是耳廓狐用來散熱的，與儲水無關。
questions.evidence: its body is able to extract enough water from the dry seeds it eats

questions.stem: The word "exerting" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: using a lot of effort or energy
questions.explain: 沙漠動物白天躲在洞裡休息、晚上才出來，是為了減少能量與水分的消耗，可知牠們避免的是在大熱天「耗費體力」，故選 (C)。(B)「降溫」正是牠們想要的，不會刻意避免。
questions.evidence: Most desert animals also avoid exerting themselves in the heat of the day.

questions.stem: Why do many desert seeds grow, flower, and drop new seeds within just a few weeks after a heavy rain?
options: Desert animals eat the flowers quickly.
They must finish before the water is gone.
The ground becomes too cold after rain.
They need the strong midday sun to grow.
questions.explain: 第四段說種子會在幾週內發芽、開花、結籽，「趕在水分消失之前」，可推知它們必須把握短暫的水分完成生命週期，故選 (B)。其他選項文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: before the water disappears

vocab.stem: The milk in the fridge has passed its ______ date, so please throw it away.
vocab.explain: 牛奶已經過了「到期」日，所以要丟掉，expiration date 指有效期限，故選 expiration。fascination（著迷）、exclusion（排除）、fertility（肥沃；生育力）都無法和 date 搭配表示期限。

vocab.stem: Students who have a doctor's note are ______ from the long-distance run in P.E. class.
vocab.explain: 有醫生證明的學生可以「免除」體育課的長跑，be exempt from 表示被豁免，故選 exempt。feasible（可行的）、extracurricular（課外的）、feminine（女性的）都不能接 from 表示免做某事。

title: Dressing Up Who You Are
paragraphs: Every morning, millions of teenagers stand in front of a closet and make a small but important decision. The [[garments|L6-0375]] we choose do more than keep us warm. They send messages about who we are, which groups we belong to, and how we want others to see us. Long before we say a single word, our clothes have already started the conversation.

This is especially true during [[adolescence|L6-0023]], when young people are still figuring out who they are. A girl who was once happy to wear whatever her parents bought may suddenly make a big [[fuss|L6-0372]] about the color of her shoes. Some parents see this as a sign of trouble, and the [[friction|L6-0368]] it causes at home can be real. Yet it is often a healthy step. Choosing your own look is one way of saying, "This is me."

Fitting in matters, too. Some students [[forsake|L6-0358]] styles they love because they fear being called a fashion [[freak|L6-0366]]. Others go through a [[frantic|L6-0365]] search for the perfect outfit before a [[forthcoming|L6-0359]] class trip, worried that the wrong jacket will make them stand out. With only a [[finite|L6-0346]] amount of pocket money, they must also decide what really matters to them.

Clothes can also connect us to the past. In Taiwan, some young designers [[fuse|L6-0371]] traditional patterns with modern designs. A few borrow patterns from Indigenous [[folklore|L6-0355]] and [[textiles|L6-0914]], working closely with Indigenous artists so that the meaning behind each pattern is respected. For many people, wearing such clothes can [[fortify|L6-0360]] a sense of where they come from.

In the end, style is [[subjective|L6-0875]]; there is no single right way to look. The task of [[formulating|L6-0357]] a personal style may seem [[formidable|L6-0356]] at first, but it does not require expensive [[accessories|L6-0008]]. It only requires paying close attention to what feels true to you, and the courage to try.
zh: 每天早上，數以百萬計的青少年站在衣櫥前，做出一個微小卻重要的決定。我們挑選的衣服不只是用來保暖，它們還傳遞了訊息：我們是誰、屬於哪些群體，以及希望別人怎麼看待我們。早在我們開口說第一句話之前，衣服就已經替我們開啟了對話。
在青春期，這一點尤其明顯，因為這時年輕人還在摸索自己是什麼樣的人。一個以前不管父母買什麼都樂意穿的女孩，可能突然為了鞋子的顏色大驚小怪。有些父母把這看成問題的徵兆，而它在家中引起的摩擦也可能是真的。不過，這往往是健康的一步。選擇自己的造型，正是表達「這就是我」的一種方式。
融入群體也很重要。有些學生放棄自己喜愛的風格，因為怕被說成時尚怪咖。也有人在即將到來的班級旅行前，瘋狂地尋找完美的穿搭，擔心穿錯外套會讓自己太顯眼。零用錢有限，他們也必須決定什麼對自己才是真正重要的。
衣服也能把我們和過去連結起來。在台灣，有些年輕設計師把傳統圖紋融入現代設計。少數設計師從原住民的傳說與織品中借用圖紋，並與原住民藝術家密切合作，讓每個圖紋背後的意義受到尊重。對許多人來說，穿上這樣的衣服能強化對自己根源的認同。
說到底，風格是主觀的，沒有唯一正確的打扮方式。建立個人風格一開始可能看似艱鉅，但並不需要昂貴的配件。只需要用心留意什麼讓你覺得最像自己，再加上一點嘗試的勇氣。

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Teenagers should follow the latest fashion closely.
Parents should choose clothes for their teenage children.
Clothes are one way people show and shape who they are.
Indigenous patterns are the most beautiful designs of all.
questions.explain: 文章從衣服傳遞「我們是誰」的訊息談起，再談青春期的自我表達、融入群體與文化認同，最後說風格是主觀的，故選 (C)。(D) 原住民圖紋只是第四段的例子。
questions.evidence: They send messages about who we are, which groups we belong to, and how we want others to see us.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, why do some students give up styles they love?
options: They have no pocket money at all.
They are afraid of being called a fashion freak.
Their school does not allow those styles.
Their friends say the styles are too expensive.
questions.explain: 第三段說有些學生放棄喜愛的風格，是因為怕被說成時尚怪咖，故選 (B)。(A) 文中說的是零用錢「有限」，並非完全沒有。
questions.evidence: because they fear being called a fashion freak

vocab.stem: As soon as the gate opened, the horses began to ______ across the open field.

title: Seeing Red, Feeling Blue
paragraphs: Why does a gray, rainy morning sometimes fill us with [[gloom|L6-0386]], while a bright yellow room seems to lift our mood? Many people believe that colors [[evoke|L6-0316]] feelings in a direct and simple way. Psychologists have studied this question for decades, and the answers are more interesting, and less simple, than most people expect.

Some links between color and feeling appear in many places. Red, the color of blood and fire, is often connected with energy, danger, and strong emotion. Blue, the color of a clear sky and a quiet sea, is often said to [[soothe|L6-0839]] the mind. Gold and silver, which [[gleam|L6-0383]] and [[glitter|L6-0385]] in the light, are widely linked to wealth and [[glamour|L6-0382]]. That is why shops selling [[glamorous|L6-0381]] products often use these colors on their signs and boxes.

However, the meaning of a color is not the same in every place. [[Geographical|L6-0378]] and cultural differences matter a great deal. In Taiwan, red stands for good luck and fills the streets during the Lunar New Year. In many Western countries, white is the [[customary|L6-0218]] color for a wedding dress, but in some parts of East Asia, white has long been worn at funerals. A color that shows [[goodwill|L6-0388]] in one place may send a sad message in another.

Scientists also warn that many popular claims about color should not be taken as [[gospel|L6-0390]]. It is hard to [[gauge|L6-0376]] the effect of a color alone, because our feelings are also shaped by memories, light, and the situation we are in. A person who loves the sea may feel peaceful in a blue room, while someone who once spent a lonely week in a blue hospital room may not.

So should you paint your study room a certain color? A color will probably not [[hamper|L6-0399]] your learning either way. Choose colors that make you feel comfortable, and try not to [[grumble|L6-0396]] if your family prefers something different. What a color means depends a lot on the person looking at it.
zh: 為什麼一個灰濛濛的雨天早晨有時會讓我們心情低落，而一間明亮的黃色房間卻好像能讓人心情變好？許多人相信，顏色會直接而簡單地喚起某些感受。心理學家研究這個問題已有數十年，得到的答案比多數人預期的更有趣，也沒那麼簡單。
有些顏色和感受之間的連結在許多地方都看得到。紅色是血與火的顏色，常和活力、危險及強烈的情緒聯想在一起。藍色是晴空與平靜大海的顏色，常被認為能讓心情平靜下來。在光線下閃閃發亮的金色和銀色，則普遍和財富與魅力有關。這就是為什麼販賣奢華商品的店家，常在招牌和包裝盒上使用這些顏色。
不過，顏色的意義並非到處都一樣。地理和文化的差異影響很大。在台灣，紅色代表好運，農曆新年期間大街小巷一片紅。在許多西方國家，白色是婚紗慣用的顏色；但在東亞某些地方，白色長久以來是喪禮上穿的顏色。一種在某地表達善意的顏色，在另一個地方可能傳達哀傷的訊息。
科學家也提醒，許多關於顏色的流行說法不該被當成絕對真理。單獨衡量一種顏色的影響並不容易，因為我們的感受也受到回憶、光線以及當下處境的影響。熱愛大海的人待在藍色房間裡可能覺得平靜，但曾經在藍色病房裡孤單度過一週的人，感受可能就不同了。
那麼，你該把讀書的房間漆成某種特定顏色嗎？無論選哪種顏色，大概都不會妨礙你的學習。選擇讓你覺得舒服的顏色就好，如果家人偏好別的顏色，也盡量別抱怨。一種顏色代表什麼，很大程度取決於看著它的那個人。

questions.stem: According to the passage, why do shops selling glamorous products often use gold and silver?

questions.explain: 科學家提醒流行說法「不該被 taken as gospel」，接著解釋顏色的影響其實很難單獨衡量，可知意思是「被當成絕對真理而全盤相信」，故選 (B)。(A) 是 gospel 字面上「福音」的聯想，不符合此處語意。

questions.stem: What would the writer most likely tell a student choosing a color for her study room?

Avoid red, because it always makes people angry.

title: Working One Task at a Time
paragraphs: With a few taps on a phone, you can [[hail|L6-0398]] a ride, order dinner, or hire someone to design a poster. Behind each of these services is a worker who is paid by the task, or "gig," rather than by the month. This way of working, often called the gig economy, has grown quickly in many countries, and it is especially attractive to young people.

For students, the biggest attraction is freedom. A university student can deliver food between classes, accept jobs only when it is [[feasible|L6-0339]], and turn the app off during exams. Some use gig work to [[diversify|L6-0272]] their income, while others treat it as a chance to try out different kinds of work before choosing a career. Getting started is usually easy, too. Often, a phone and a bicycle are all that is needed.

Yet this freedom comes at a price. In many places, gig workers are treated as people running their own small businesses rather than as employees. As a result, they may receive no sick pay or health insurance, and they must cover their own [[expenditure|L6-0325]] on fuel, repairs, and phone bills. Income is hard to [[gauge|L6-0376]] in advance because it rises and falls with demand. Delivery workers may rush through [[frantic|L6-0365]] traffic to finish orders on time, and a single low rating from a customer can [[hamper|L6-0399]] their chances of getting more work. Some [[grumble|L6-0396]] that they feel [[dispensable|L6-0263]]: if they stop working, the app simply sends the job to someone else.

For young workers, these problems can be [[magnified|L6-0535]]. With little work experience, they may not fully understand the rules they agree to when they sign up. Many [[exert|L6-0324]] themselves for long hours without realizing how little they earn once costs are taken away. When a customer treats them rudely, or when [[harassment|L6-0402]] happens, they may have no manager to turn to.

None of this means that gig work should be avoided. Many customers show [[goodwill|L6-0388]] by leaving kind reviews, and many workers value the chance to earn money on their own schedule. The key is to go in with open eyes: read the rules carefully, keep track of every cost, and see gig work as one step on a longer path, not the whole journey.
zh: 只要在手機上點幾下，你就能叫車、點晚餐，或是請人設計一張海報。每一項服務的背後，都有一位按件計酬的工作者，他們領的是每一件任務的報酬，也就是所謂的「零工」，而不是月薪。這種工作方式常被稱為「零工經濟」，在許多國家快速成長，對年輕人尤其有吸引力。
對學生來說，最大的吸引力在於自由。大學生可以在課堂之間外送餐點，只在可行的時候接單，考試期間就把應用程式關掉。有些人用零工讓收入來源多樣化，也有人把它當作選擇職業前試做不同工作的機會。而且入門通常很容易，往往只需要一支手機和一輛腳踏車。
然而，這份自由是有代價的。在許多地方，零工工作者被視為自己經營小生意的人，而不是受雇員工。因此，他們可能沒有病假工資或健康保險，還得自行負擔油錢、維修費和手機費等支出。收入很難事先估計，因為它會隨著需求起伏。外送員可能要在混亂的車陣中趕著準時送達，而顧客的一次低評分就可能妨礙他們接到更多工作。有些人抱怨覺得自己可有可無：只要他們不做了，應用程式就直接把工作派給別人。
對年輕工作者來說，這些問題可能會被放大。由於工作經驗不多，他們註冊時可能並不完全了解自己同意的規則。許多人長時間賣力工作，卻沒有發現扣掉成本之後自己其實賺得多麼少。當顧客態度惡劣，或發生騷擾事件時，他們可能沒有主管可以求助。
這並不表示應該避開零工。許多顧客會留下友善的評價來表達善意，許多工作者也很珍惜能依照自己時間賺錢的機會。關鍵在於睜大眼睛投入：仔細閱讀規則、記下每一筆成本，並把零工看作漫長道路上的一步，而不是旅程的全部。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to become a successful delivery worker
The good and bad sides of gig work, especially for young people
Why phone apps have become so popular
Why customers should always leave kind reviews
questions.explain: 文章先介紹零工經濟及它對學生的吸引力，再談沒有保障、收入不穩等問題，以及年輕人特別面臨的風險，最後提出建議，故選 (B)。(D) 留下友善評價只是最後一段的一個例子。

questions.stem: Why might some gig workers feel "dispensable"?

They earn much more than other workers.

questions.stem: The word "magnified" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 第四段接著說年輕人經驗不足、可能不了解規則、沒有主管可求助，表示前一段的問題對他們來說更嚴重，所以 magnified 指「被放大、變得更嚴重」，故選 (C)。(A)「解決」與後文描述的困境相反。

vocab.stem: Before cooking, she rubbed a little ______ on the pan so that the eggs would not stick to it.
vocab.explain: 下鍋前在平底鍋上抹一點東西，讓蛋不會黏鍋，應是「油脂」，故選 grease。glamour（魅力）、gloom（陰暗；憂鬱）、gospel（福音）都不是能抹在鍋子上的東西。

vocab.stem: If you leave the bread out on the table overnight, it will ______ and become difficult to chew.
vocab.explain: 麵包放在桌上一整晚會「變硬」而難以咀嚼，故選 harden。glide（滑行）、hail（下冰雹；招呼）、grumble（抱怨）都不能說明麵包為何變得難咬。

title: The Scissors Inside a Cell
paragraphs: Bacteria have fought viruses for billions of years. A virus [[hijacks|L6-0417]] a cell, forcing it to make copies of the virus. To defend themselves, many bacteria keep a kind of memory: small pieces of virus DNA stored in their own genes. If the same virus attacks again, the bacteria use this memory to find the virus's DNA and cut it apart.

Researchers had a [[hunch|L6-0427]] that this system could be useful. In 2012, a team including Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier showed how to [[harness|L6-0405]] it as a tool. Known as CRISPR, the tool can be guided to almost any spot in a cell's DNA to cut it, so that scientists can remove or change genes. The discovery [[illuminated|L6-0433]] a faster and cheaper path to gene editing, and in 2020 the two women received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

The tool has already changed lives. People with sickle cell disease, a blood disease caused by a [[defect|L6-0227]] in a single gene, often suffer sudden, terrible pain and may need to be [[hospitalized|L6-0423]] again and again. In 2023, a treatment based on CRISPR was approved in the UK and the United States. The first patients who tested such treatments showed [[heroic|L6-0413]] courage, and for some, years of pain have ended.

Yet the same power [[heightens|L6-0411]] serious worries. Changing the genes of a sick adult affects only that person. Changing the genes of an embryo, however, can affect every future generation that comes from it. In 2018, a researcher in China announced that he had edited the genes of twin babies before birth. Scientists around the world criticized him, saying that the risks were not yet understood and that no one could be held [[accountable|L6-0012]] for harm to future generations.

Most scientists agree that treating sick adults, when [[deemed|L6-0225]] safe, is a great gift. Far fewer support editing embryos. Many questions still [[hover|L6-0425]] over the field, and when asked where the line should be, experts often [[hedge|L6-0410]] their answers. Today's questions may be only the tip of the [[iceberg|L6-0432]], and they belong not just to scientists but to all of us.
zh: 細菌和病毒已經對抗了數十億年。病毒會劫持細胞，逼它製造病毒的複製品。為了保護自己，許多細菌保有一種「記憶」：把一小段一小段的病毒 DNA 存在自己的基因裡。同一種病毒再次來襲時，細菌就利用這份記憶找到病毒的 DNA，把它剪斷。
研究人員直覺認為這套系統可能很有用。2012 年，包括珍妮佛・道納和艾曼紐・夏彭蒂耶在內的團隊展示了如何把它當成工具加以利用。這項工具稱為 CRISPR，可以被引導到細胞 DNA 上幾乎任何位置進行剪切，讓科學家能移除或改變基因。這項發現為基因編輯開闢了一條更快、更便宜的路，兩位女科學家也在 2020 年獲得諾貝爾化學獎。
這項工具已經改變了一些人的生命。鐮刀型紅血球疾病是由單一基因缺陷造成的血液疾病，患者常會突然劇烈疼痛，可能需要一次又一次住院。2023 年，一種以 CRISPR 為基礎的療法在英國和美國獲得核准。最早參與試驗這類療法的病患展現了英勇的勇氣，其中有些人多年的疼痛已經結束。
然而，同樣的力量也加深了嚴重的疑慮。改變一位成年病人的基因，只會影響那個人；但改變胚胎的基因，卻可能影響由它而來的每一個後代。2018 年，中國一名研究人員宣布，他在一對雙胞胎出生前編輯了她們的基因。世界各地的科學家紛紛批評他，指出相關風險尚未被了解，而且一旦對後代造成傷害，沒有人能為此負責。
多數科學家都同意，在被認定安全的情況下治療成年病人是一份珍貴的禮物；支持編輯胚胎的人則少得多。這個領域仍籠罩著許多問題，當被問到界線應該畫在哪裡時，專家往往會含糊其辭。今天的問題可能只是冰山一角，而這些問題不只屬於科學家，也屬於我們每一個人。

questions.stem: How do bacteria use the small pieces of virus DNA they store?
options: To make copies of the virus
To change the color of their cells
As a memory to find and cut the same virus later
questions.explain: 第一段說細菌把病毒 DNA 片段存起來當作記憶，同一種病毒再來時就用它找到病毒 DNA 並剪斷，故選 (C)。(A) 製造病毒複製品是病毒劫持細胞後逼細胞做的事。
questions.evidence: the bacteria use this memory to find the virus's DNA and cut it apart

questions.stem: What happened in 2023, according to the passage?
options: A treatment based on CRISPR was approved in the UK and the United States.
A researcher edited the genes of twin babies.
Doudna and Charpentier won the Nobel Prize.
Scientists first found the memory system in bacteria.
questions.explain: 第三段說 2023 年一種以 CRISPR 為基礎的療法在英國和美國獲得核准，故選 (A)。(C) 得獎是 2020 年，(B) 編輯雙胞胎基因是 2018 年。
questions.evidence: In 2023, a treatment based on CRISPR was approved in the UK and the United States.

questions.stem: Why do far fewer scientists support editing embryos than treating sick adults?
options: Embryos cannot be studied in a laboratory.
Editing embryos costs much more money.
Sick adults do not need gene editing.
Changes made to an embryo can be passed on to future generations.
questions.explain: 第四段說改變成人基因只影響本人，改變胚胎基因卻可能影響之後的每一代，而風險尚未被了解，可推知這是科學家較不支持編輯胚胎的原因，故選 (D)。(B) 文中沒有提到費用。
questions.evidence: can affect every future generation that comes from it

questions.stem: The word "hedge" in paragraph 5 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 前文說這個領域仍籠罩著許多問題，被問到界線在哪裡時，專家往往 hedge their answers，可知是「含糊其辭、不明確表態」，故選 (B)。(D) 與專家謹慎的態度相反。
