title: When Night Stopped Being Dark
paragraphs: For most of human history, the sun decided when the day ended. After [[dusk|L6-0288]], people had only fires and candles, which were dim and costly, so most went to bed not long after dark. Then, in 1879, Thomas Edison introduced a practical electric light bulb. Within a few decades, electric lights had become a [[staple|L6-0856]] of city life, and streets were [[illuminated|L6-0433]] all night long. For the first time, night was no longer truly dark.

Our bodies, however, have not kept up with this change. Inside the brain, a natural clock follows a cycle of roughly twenty-four hours. As evening falls, the body releases a hormone called melatonin, which helps us feel sleepy. Bright light, especially the blue light from phones and computer screens, sends the opposite signal. It acts as a kind of [[stimulation|L6-0866]], telling the brain that it is still day and [[spurring|L6-0853]] us to stay awake.

Teenagers may suffer the most. During [[adolescence|L6-0023]], the body clock naturally shifts later, so many teens do not feel sleepy until late at night. Add an hour of [[scrolling|L6-0790]] in bed, and sleep may be pushed back even further. The next morning, a tired student may [[stagger|L6-0855]] to the bus stop and struggle to focus in class.

The good news is that small changes can help [[stabilize|L6-0854]] the body clock. Experts suggest dimming the lights an hour before bed and keeping phones out of the bedroom. Many [[stylish|L6-0874]] lamps now offer warm, soft colors meant for evening use. Even [[stray|L6-0869]] light from a street lamp can disturb sleep, so thick curtains may help. Morning light matters, too: a short [[stroll|L6-0871]] outdoors after breakfast tells the brain that the day has begun.

Artificial light has allowed humans to make great [[strides|L6-0870]]; we can study, work, and enjoy ourselves long after the sun goes down. But if you [[subscribe|L6-0877]] to the idea that sleep is a waste of time, think again. It is time to give sleep the [[spotlight|L6-0852]] it deserves.
zh: 在人類歷史的大部分時間裡，一天何時結束是由太陽決定的。黃昏過後，人們只有火光和蠟燭可用，既昏暗又昂貴，所以大多數人天黑後不久就上床睡覺。後來在 1879 年，愛迪生推出了實用的電燈泡。短短幾十年內，電燈成了城市生活不可或缺的一部分，街道整夜燈火通明。夜晚第一次不再真正黑暗。
然而，我們的身體並沒有跟上這個改變。大腦中有一個天然的時鐘，大約以二十四小時為一個週期運作。傍晚來臨時，身體會分泌一種叫褪黑激素的荷爾蒙，幫助我們產生睡意。明亮的光線，尤其是手機和電腦螢幕發出的藍光，卻會送出相反的訊號。它就像一種刺激，告訴大腦現在還是白天，促使我們保持清醒。
青少年受到的影響可能最大。在青春期，身體的時鐘自然會往後延，所以許多青少年要到深夜才會想睡。如果再加上在床上滑一個小時的手機，入睡時間可能會被推得更晚。隔天早上，疲倦的學生可能腳步搖晃地走到公車站，上課時也很難專心。
好消息是，一些小改變就能幫助身體時鐘穩定下來。專家建議在睡前一小時把燈光調暗，並且不要把手機帶進臥室。現在許多時尚的檯燈也提供適合晚上使用的溫暖柔和色調。就連路燈射進來的零星光線也可能干擾睡眠，所以厚窗簾或許有幫助。早晨的光線也很重要：早餐後到戶外散步一小段，就能告訴大腦新的一天已經開始了。
人造光讓人類得以大步向前；太陽下山後很久，我們仍能讀書、工作和娛樂。不過，如果你認同睡覺是浪費時間的想法，請再想一想。是時候讓睡眠得到它應有的關注了。

title: The Power of "Not Yet"
paragraphs: Some students see a low test score as a final verdict: "I'm just bad at math." Others see it as useful information: "I haven't learned this yet." According to Stanford psychologist Carol Dweck, this difference reflects two kinds of mindset. People with a "fixed mindset" believe that ability is something you either have or lack. People with a "growth mindset" believe that ability can be developed through effort, good methods, and help from others.

In a well-known set of experiments in the 1990s, Dweck and a colleague gave children some puzzles to solve. Afterward, some children were praised for being smart, while others were praised for working hard. When later offered a choice, many of the children praised for intelligence picked easy tasks that would protect their image. Those praised for effort were more willing to try harder problems. To the first group, it seemed, "smart" had become a [[synonym|L6-0903]] for "never making mistakes."

A fixed mindset often leads to [[superficial|L6-0885]] learning. Students may memorize answers just to enjoy a feeling of [[superiority|L6-0887]] over their classmates, only to feel [[swamped|L6-0897]] when the problems become difficult. Practice seems [[tedious|L6-0907]], and every mistake feels like proof of failure.

Someone with a growth mindset, on the other hand, can [[summon|L6-0884]] the courage to [[persevere|L6-0660]]. To her, mistakes [[symbolize|L6-0899]] progress rather than defeat, and each [[hurdle|L6-0428]] is a chance to learn. Through [[successive|L6-0881]] attempts, her skills slowly build, and one day she may [[surpass|L6-0894]] even her own expectations. That [[surge|L6-0891]] of pride is the reward for her hard work.

Later research has found that mindset lessons alone help some students more than others, so a growth mindset is not magic. Still, the way we explain our failures matters. If a friend is upset about a poor grade, you can [[sympathize|L6-0901]] with her and then remind her of one powerful word: "yet." With effort, she may [[attain|L6-0065]] what once seemed out of reach.
zh: 有些學生把一次考不好看成最終判決：「我就是數學不好。」也有學生把它看成有用的資訊：「這個我還沒學會。」史丹佛大學心理學家卡蘿・杜維克認為，這種差異反映出兩種心態。抱持「定型心態」的人相信能力是天生的，有就有、沒有就沒有；抱持「成長心態」的人則相信，能力可以透過努力、好的方法和別人的幫助來培養。
在 1990 年代一系列知名的實驗中，杜維克和一位同事讓孩子解一些謎題。之後，有些孩子被誇獎很聰明，另一些則被誇獎很努力。後來讓他們選擇時，許多被誇聰明的孩子挑了簡單的題目，以維護自己的形象；被誇努力的孩子則比較願意挑戰更難的問題。對第一組孩子來說，「聰明」似乎成了「從不犯錯」的同義詞。
定型心態常常導致膚淺的學習。學生可能只是為了享受勝過同學的優越感而背答案，等到題目變難時，卻覺得難以招架。練習顯得乏味，每一個錯誤都像是失敗的證據。
相反地，擁有成長心態的人能夠鼓起勇氣堅持下去。對她來說，錯誤象徵的是進步而不是挫敗，每一道關卡都是學習的機會。經過一次又一次的嘗試，她的能力慢慢累積，總有一天可能超越自己原本的期待。那股湧上心頭的自豪，就是她努力的回報。
後來的研究發現，光是上心態課程，對某些學生的幫助比較大，所以成長心態並不是萬靈丹。儘管如此，我們如何解釋自己的失敗仍然很重要。如果朋友為了成績不好而難過，你可以同理她的感受，再提醒她一個很有力量的詞：「還沒」。只要努力，她或許就能達成過去看似遙不可及的目標。

questions.evidence: so a growth mindset is not magic

vocab.stem: Washing the same dishes every night can feel ______, but listening to music makes the job more fun.
vocab.explain: 每晚洗同樣的碗盤，but 後面說聽音樂會讓它比較有趣，可知原本很「乏味的」，故選 tedious。superficial（膚淺的）、superstitious（迷信的）、surgical（外科的）都不符合句意。

vocab.stem: Before her first speech in English, Lin had to ______ all her courage to walk onto the stage.
vocab.explain: 第一次上台用英文演講，需要「鼓起」所有勇氣，summon one's courage 是常見搭配，故選 summon。surpass（超越）、symbolize（象徵）、sympathize（同情）都不能和 courage 這樣搭配。

title: Shadows Across Distant Suns
paragraphs: Why do stars [[twinkle|L6-0937]]? After traveling [[trillions|L6-0930]] of kilometers through space, their light is bent by moving air in Earth's atmosphere just before it reaches our eyes. For thousands of years, people could only wonder whether those tiny points of light had planets of their own. The telescope began to change that. In 1610, Galileo pointed one at Jupiter and discovered four moons circling it, clear evidence that not everything in the sky [[revolves|L6-0770]] around Earth.

Finding planets around other stars was far harder. A planet gives off no light of its own, and it is lost in the glare of its star, like a candle placed beside a lighthouse. For a long time, every claim was [[tentative|L6-0912]] at best. Then, in 1995, two Swiss [[astronomers|L6-0063]] announced the first planet found circling a sun-like star. Not long [[thereafter|L6-0915]], the [[tempo|L6-0910]] of discovery picked up, and new planets began to arrive in a [[torrent|L6-0922]].

One popular method is to watch for a "transit." When a planet passes in front of its star, the star's light dims very slightly. Measuring such tiny changes night after night would be [[tiresome|L6-0919]] for humans, but computers do much of the work. The method works only when a planet's path is [[tilted|L6-0917]] at just the right angle as seen from Earth. NASA's Kepler space telescope, launched in 2009, watched about 150,000 stars at once and helped find thousands of planets.

Today more than five thousand planets beyond our solar system are known. Some are giant balls of gas; others are rocky worlds that might hold water. Scientists are far from [[unanimous|L6-0938]] about whether life exists on any of them, but the search continues. The [[trek|L6-0928]] to even the nearest star would take a [[spacecraft|L6-0842]] from Earth tens of thousands of years, so for now, astronomers explore with light alone. The next time you watch the first stars appear at [[twilight|L6-0936]], remember that many of them probably have worlds of their own.
zh: 星星為什麼會閃爍？星光穿越太空、走了好幾兆公里，就在快要抵達我們眼睛之前，被地球大氣中流動的空氣折射了。數千年來，人們只能猜想那些微小的光點是否也有自己的行星。望遠鏡開始改變了這一切。1610 年，伽利略把望遠鏡對準木星，發現有四顆衛星繞著它轉，這清楚證明了天上的東西並不都是繞著地球轉的。
要找到繞著其他恆星運行的行星就困難多了。行星本身不發光，又淹沒在恆星的強光裡，就像擺在燈塔旁的一根蠟燭。很長一段時間，每一個發現行星的說法頂多只能算是暫定的。後來在 1995 年，兩位瑞士天文學家宣布找到第一顆繞著類似太陽的恆星運行的行星。此後不久，發現的步調加快，新行星如潮水般湧現。
一種常用的方法是觀察「凌日」。當行星從恆星前方經過時，恆星的亮度會非常輕微地變暗。對人類來說，夜復一夜地測量這麼微小的變化會很累人，但電腦能完成大部分的工作。這種方法只有在行星的軌道從地球看去恰好傾斜在適當角度時才有效。美國太空總署於 2009 年發射的克卜勒太空望遠鏡同時監看約十五萬顆恆星，協助找到了數千顆行星。
如今，太陽系外已知的行星超過五千顆。有些是巨大的氣體球，有些則是可能有水的岩石世界。對於這些行星上是否存在生命，科學家的看法還遠遠沒有一致，但搜尋仍在持續。從地球出發的太空船即使只是前往最近的恆星，也要花上數萬年，所以目前天文學家只能靠光來探索。下次你在黃昏看著第一批星星出現時，記得它們之中許多可能都有屬於自己的世界。

questions.stem: Why do stars twinkle?
options: They give off light that keeps changing color.
Planets keep passing in front of them.
They are moving away from Earth.
Moving air in Earth's atmosphere bends their light.
questions.explain: 第一段說星光快抵達我們眼睛之前，被地球大氣中流動的空氣折射，所以會閃爍，故選 (D)。(B) 行星經過恆星前方是第三段介紹的「凌日」現象。
questions.evidence: their light is bent by moving air in Earth's atmosphere

questions.stem: What happens during a "transit"?
options: A planet passes in front of its star, and the star's light dims slightly.
A star moves to a new place in the sky.
A spacecraft lands on another planet.
Two stars crash into each other.
questions.explain: 第三段說行星從恆星前方經過時，恆星的亮度會非常輕微地變暗，這就是凌日，故選 (A)。其他選項文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: When a planet passes in front of its star, the star's light dims very slightly.

questions.stem: The phrase "in a torrent" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 前文說發現的步調加快，可知新行星像「洪流」般大量湧現，故選 (B)。(C) 一次一顆與步調加快的意思相反。
questions.evidence: new planets began to arrive in a torrent

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
options: Humans will soon travel to the nearest star.
Scientists have already found life on another planet.
For now, studying light is the main way to learn about distant planets.
Most stars have no planets at all.
questions.explain: 最後一段說到最近的恆星也要數萬年，所以目前天文學家只能靠光來探索，故選 (C)。(B) 文中說科學家對是否有生命看法並不一致；(D) 與文末「許多星星可能都有自己的世界」相反。
questions.evidence: so for now, astronomers explore with light alone

vocab.stem: As the small plane flew into strong winds, it began to ______ to one side, and several passengers grabbed their seats.
vocab.explain: 飛機遇到強風，往一側「傾斜」，乘客才會抓緊座位，故選 tilt。trek（長途跋涉）、twinkle（閃爍）、tiptoe（踮腳走）都不能描述飛機的動作。

vocab.stem: The committee's decision was ______: all twelve members voted yes.
vocab.explain: 十二位成員全部投贊成票，表示決定是「全體一致的」，故選 unanimous。tentative（暫定的）、tiresome（令人厭煩的）、tropic（熱帶的）都不符合冒號後的說明。

title: Packing for Mars
paragraphs: When a rocket lifts off, the [[astronauts|L6-0062]] inside feel the whole craft [[vibrate|L6-0964]] as powerful engines [[propel|L6-0702]] it [[upward|L6-0949]] through the atmosphere. For decades, such launches were rare and extremely expensive, partly because most rockets could be used only once. Today, some companies land their rockets [[upright|L6-0947]] on a pad or a ship at sea so that they can fly again, and the cost of reaching space has fallen greatly.

Plans to go farther are already [[underway|L6-0943]]. NASA's Artemis program aims to land astronauts on the moon again for the first time since 1972, and several countries have [[unveiled|L6-0946]] plans to build bases there. Mars is the next goal. A trip there would take about six to nine months each way, and crews would have to [[navigate|L6-0586]] millions of kilometers of empty space, far from any hospital if something went wrong.

Engineers warn that we should not [[underestimate|L6-0940]] the challenges of daily life on such a journey. Every [[utensil|L6-0953]], tool, and piece of clothing must earn its place, so designers look for [[versatile|L6-0961]] items that can serve many purposes. Water is too heavy to carry in large amounts, so it must be used again and again. On the International Space Station, machines already collect water [[vapor|L6-0958]] from the air, including moisture from the astronauts' breath and sweat, and turn it back into clean drinking water.

Some scientists feel a sense of [[urgency|L6-0951]] about this work. Learning to live on other worlds could also teach us to take better care of our own, from growing food with very little water to producing energy without pollution. [[Underneath|L6-0941]] the excitement, however, lie serious questions about cost and safety that have no easy answers.

Perhaps the greatest gift of space travel is the view of home. Many astronauts say that seeing Earth from above, a small blue ball [[veiled|L6-0959]] in thin white clouds, left them so amazed that they could hardly [[utter|L6-0954]] a word. From that distance, the planet looks like one shared home. Such a view may help [[unify|L6-0945]] people who share the same small world.
zh: 火箭升空時，裡面的太空人會感覺整架火箭在震動，強大的引擎推動它向上穿越大氣層。幾十年來，這樣的發射次數很少，而且極其昂貴，部分原因是大多數火箭只能使用一次。如今，有些公司讓火箭直立降落在發射台上或海上的船上，以便再次飛行，進入太空的成本也因此大幅下降。
前往更遠處的計畫已經在進行中。美國太空總署的阿提米絲計畫，目標是讓太空人自 1972 年以來首度再次登陸月球；也有好幾個國家公布了在月球上建立基地的計畫。火星則是下一個目標。單程前往火星大約需要六到九個月，太空人必須在數百萬公里的空曠太空中航行，萬一出事，離任何醫院都非常遙遠。
工程師提醒，我們不應低估這種旅程中日常生活的挑戰。每一件餐具、工具和衣物都必須有存在的價值，所以設計師尋找能有多種用途的多功能物品。水太重了，無法大量攜帶，因此必須一再重複使用。在國際太空站上，機器已經能從空氣中收集水蒸氣，包括太空人呼吸和汗水中的水分，再把它變回乾淨的飲用水。
有些科學家對這項工作抱有一種急迫感。學習在其他星球上生活，也能教我們更好地照顧自己的星球，從用很少的水種植糧食，到不產生污染地生產能源都是。然而，在興奮之下，還潛藏著關於成本與安全的嚴肅問題，而且沒有簡單的答案。
太空旅行最珍貴的禮物，也許是回望家園的景象。許多太空人說，從上方看見地球——一顆被薄薄白雲籠罩的藍色小球——讓他們驚嘆得幾乎說不出話來。從那樣的距離看，這顆星球就像一個共同的家。這樣的景象，或許能讓共享這個小小世界的人們更加團結。

questions.stem: Why has the cost of reaching space fallen?
options: Some rockets land upright and can be used again.
Rockets no longer need powerful engines.
questions.explain: 第一段說過去火箭大多只能用一次，如今有些公司讓火箭直立降落以便再次飛行，成本因此大幅下降，故選 (B)。其他選項文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: some companies land their rockets upright on a pad or a ship at sea so that they can fly again

questions.stem: How does the International Space Station get some of its drinking water?
options: It brings fresh water from Earth every week.
It melts ice found on the moon.
Machines collect water vapor from the air and clean it.
Astronauts collect rain during the journey.
questions.explain: 第三段說國際太空站的機器能從空氣中收集水蒸氣，包括呼吸和汗水中的水分，再變回乾淨的飲用水，故選 (C)。(A) 文中說水太重，無法大量攜帶。
questions.evidence: machines already collect water vapor from the air

questions.stem: The word "versatile" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 後面的 that can serve many purposes 說明這些物品能有多種用途，所以 versatile 指「多功能的」，故選 (A)。(D) 很重正是太空旅行想避免的。
questions.evidence: versatile items that can serve many purposes

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, how might space travel benefit people on Earth?
options: It will allow everyone to leave Earth.
It will end all pollution right away.
Seeing Earth from space may make people feel they share one home.
questions.explain: 最後一段說從太空看地球就像一個共同的家，這樣的景象或許能讓人們更團結，故選 (D)。(C) 文中只說可能學到不產生污染的能源生產方式，並沒有說能立刻終結污染。
questions.evidence: From that distance, the planet looks like one shared home.

vocab.stem: Please do not ______ the difficulty of the climb; many hikers turn back long before they reach the top.
vocab.explain: 許多登山客還沒到山頂就折返，表示這段路很難，提醒大家不要「低估」它的難度，故選 underestimate。unveil（揭幕；公布）、unify（統一）、utter（說出）都無法搭配「難度」表達此意。

vocab.stem: This ______ pocket knife can cut rope, open cans, and tighten screws, so campers love it.
vocab.explain: 一把小刀能割繩子、開罐頭、鎖螺絲，表示它是「多功能的」，故選 versatile。upward（向上的）、unconditional（無條件的）、upright（直立的）都不能說明這些用途。

title: Graduation Day Program
paragraphs:
Green Hill Senior High School
Graduation Ceremony for the Class of 2027
Saturday, June 12, 9:30 a.m., School [[Auditorium|L6-0068]]

Dear graduates, families, and friends,
Welcome! Today we celebrate 312 students who have reached the end of one journey and the start of another. For three years, these students have brought energy and [[vitality|L6-0976]] to our campus, from sports days to club fairs. Some will now go on to university, some will enter [[vocational|L6-0978]] programs to learn a trade, and others will join the [[workforce|L6-0996]] right away. Whatever path they choose, we hope each of them finds a true [[vocation|L6-0977]]: work that feels less like a job and more like a calling. We wish them health, [[vigor|L6-0968]], and courage in the years ahead.

Order of Events
9:30 Opening music by the school orchestra, with student [[violinist|L6-0974]] Chen Yu-han
9:45 Welcome speech by Principal Grace Lin
10:00 Student speech by Lisa Wang: "Questions Worth [[Wrestling|L6-0997]] With"
10:20 Guest speech by Dr. Helen Ho, a [[veterinarian|L6-0962]] and former student: "Finding the Work You [[Yearn|L6-0999]] to Do"
10:40 Presentation of diplomas
11:30 Closing song

Important Notes
Guests: Please [[withhold|L6-0993]] applause until all the graduates in each class have received their diplomas, so that every name can be heard. You are welcome to take photos from your seat. Our staff camera operators will [[zoom|L6-1002]] in on each graduate as he or she crosses the stage, and the pictures will be shown on the large screens.
Graduates: Please arrive in Room 105 by 8:45 a.m. to line up. Hang your gown up the night before so that it will be free of [[wrinkles|L6-0998]]. [[Sneakers|L6-0826]] are fine, but please choose dark colors.

After the Ceremony
[[Refreshments|L6-0741]], including fresh fruit, [[walnut|L6-0981]] cookies, and [[yogurt|L6-1001]] cups, will be served in the [[courtyard|L6-0199]]. Our school mascot, Pecky the [[Woodpecker|L6-0995]], will be there for photos. Congratulations, Class of 2027!
zh:
綠丘高級中學
2027 級畢業典禮
6 月 12 日（星期六）上午 9:30，學校禮堂

親愛的畢業生、家長與親友們：
歡迎各位！今天我們要為 312 位同學慶祝，他們走完了一段旅程，也即將展開另一段旅程。三年來，從運動會到社團博覽會，這些同學為校園帶來了活力與朝氣。有些人將進入大學，有些人會就讀職業訓練課程學習一技之長，也有人將直接投入職場。無論選擇哪一條路，我們都希望每位同學找到真正的志業：讓人感覺不只是一份工作，而是一種使命。祝福他們在未來的日子裡健康、充滿活力，並且勇敢無懼。

典禮流程
9:30 開場音樂：學校管弦樂團演出，由學生小提琴手陳宥涵擔綱
9:45 校長林葛瑞絲致歡迎詞
10:00 學生代表王麗莎致詞：「值得好好思索的問題」
10:20 貴賓致詞：獸醫、本校校友何海倫博士：「找到你渴望從事的工作」
10:40 頒發畢業證書
11:30 唱畢業歌

注意事項
來賓：請等到每一班的畢業生全部領完證書後再鼓掌，讓每個名字都能被聽見。歡迎在座位上拍照。本校攝影人員會在每位畢業生走過舞台時拉近鏡頭拍攝，照片將顯示在大螢幕上。
畢業生：請於上午 8:45 前到 105 教室集合排隊。請在前一晚把畢業袍掛好，以免出現皺褶。可以穿運動鞋，但請選擇深色款式。

典禮結束後
中庭將提供茶點，包括新鮮水果、核桃餅乾和優格杯。本校吉祥物啄木鳥「啄啄」也會在現場陪大家拍照。恭喜 2027 級的畢業生們！

questions.stem: What time does Dr. Helen Ho's speech begin?
questions.explain: 典禮流程中寫明 10:20 是何海倫博士的貴賓致詞，故選 (D)。10:00 是學生代表王麗莎致詞。
questions.evidence: 10:20 Guest speech by Dr. Helen Ho

questions.stem: What are guests asked to do while the diplomas are being presented?
options: Stand near the stage to take better photos
Wait to clap until everyone in a class has received a diploma
questions.explain: 注意事項請來賓等到每一班畢業生都領完證書後再鼓掌，好讓每個名字都能被聽見，故選 (B)。(A) 文中請來賓在座位上拍照。
questions.evidence: Please withhold applause until all the graduates in each class have received their diplomas

questions.stem: The word "vocation" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: work that a person feels truly suited for
questions.explain: 冒號後說明 vocation 是「感覺不只是一份工作，而是一種使命」的工作，也就是「志業、天職」，故選 (A)。(B) 長假是 vacation，拼法相近但意思不同。
questions.evidence: finds a true vocation: work that feels less like a job and more like a calling

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of this text?
options: To advertise the school to new students
To report the results of a speech contest
To give information about a graduation ceremony
To ask families to give money to the school
questions.explain: 全文包含典禮時間地點、致詞、流程、給來賓和畢業生的注意事項以及典禮後的安排，目的是提供畢業典禮的資訊，故選 (C)。(B) 文中的致詞並不是比賽。
questions.evidence: Graduation Ceremony for the Class of 2027

vocab.stem: The store refused to repair Kevin's broken laptop for free because the one-year ______ had already expired.
vocab.explain: 商店不肯免費修理，是因為一年的「保固」已經過期，故選 warranty。wardrobe（衣櫥）、woe（悲痛）、vowel（母音）都不會「過期」，也與免費維修無關。

vocab.stem: Even at eighty, Grandma still practices ______ every morning, slowly stretching her body on a mat.
vocab.explain: 每天早上在墊子上慢慢伸展身體，是在練「瑜伽」，practice yoga 是常見用法，故選 yoga。villa（別墅）、yogurt（優格）、wharf（碼頭）都不能「練習」。

title: What the Stars Remember
paragraphs: At last, the travelers reach the top of the starry tower. The final [[stride|L6-0870]] onto the roof leaves them out of breath, and for a moment no one can [[utter|L6-0954]] a word. As the last light of [[twilight|L6-0936]] fades, the whole journey lies below them: the harbor where they set out, the forest where they lost and found their way, the busy port city, and the snowy mountain whose winds nearly sent them home. Above them, the stars begin to [[twinkle|L6-0937]].

Looking up, one traveler remembers a simple fact: the light from the stars is old. On dark nights, the Andromeda Galaxy appears as a faint, cloudy spot. Its light began its [[trek|L6-0928]] about two and a half million years ago, long before modern humans appeared on Earth. The night sky is not a picture of the present but a message from the past that has only just arrived.

Learning words works in a similar way. Each new word the travelers met seemed small and faint at first, a single point of light. Through [[successive|L6-0881]] lessons, those points grew in number. Some came easily; others they had to [[wrestle|L6-0997]] with again and again, and some nights their progress felt [[tentative|L6-0912]] and slow. But words, like stars, are rarely seen alone. Together they form patterns, and suddenly a sentence that once seemed dark is [[radiant|L6-0720]] with meaning.

Of course, reaching the top does not mean the journey is over. Soon the real test will arrive: the college entrance exam, and after it a world of books and dreams written in many languages. There may be moments of [[turmoil|L6-0935]] and doubt. When they come, the travelers can remember how high they have [[ascended|L6-0057]]. The [[vigor|L6-0968]] they found on the snowy mountain and the patience they learned in the forest are now part of who they are.

Before they head down, the travelers make one last wish. They [[yearn|L6-0999]] not simply for high scores but for a life of curiosity: to keep reading, keep asking, and keep looking [[upward|L6-0949]]. The stars will still be shining long after tonight, and so will every word they have learned. The tower, they realize, does not [[symbolize|L6-0899]] the end of the road. It is a place to see how far the road can go.
zh: 旅人們終於抵達星空高塔的頂端。踏上屋頂的最後一大步讓他們上氣不接下氣，有好一會兒誰都說不出話來。暮光的最後一抹亮光漸漸褪去，整段旅程就鋪展在他們腳下：當初出發的港口、他們迷路又找到方向的森林、熱鬧的港都，還有那座寒風差點把他們吹回家的雪山。在他們頭頂上，星星開始閃爍。
抬頭仰望時，一位旅人想起一個簡單的事實：星星的光是古老的。在非常暗的夜晚，仙女座星系看起來是一團模糊的雲狀光點。它的光大約在兩百五十萬年前就踏上旅程，遠在現代人類出現於地球之前。夜空並不是現在的畫面，而是一則來自過去、剛剛才抵達的訊息。
學單字也是類似的道理。旅人們一路上遇見的每個新單字，起初都顯得又小又模糊，只是一個光點。經過一課又一課，這些光點越來越多。有些單字輕鬆就記住了；有些則必須一再和它們奮鬥，有些夜晚進步顯得遲疑又緩慢。但單字就像星星，很少單獨出現。它們會連成圖案，突然之間，一個原本晦暗難懂的句子就充滿了意義的光芒。
當然，登上塔頂並不代表旅程結束。真正的考驗很快就會到來：大學入學考試，而考試之後，還有一個充滿書本和用各種語言寫成的夢想的世界。也許會有混亂與懷疑的時刻。當這些時刻來臨時，旅人們可以想想自己已經攀登得多高。他們在雪山上找到的活力，以及在森林中學會的耐心，現在都已成為他們的一部分。
下塔之前，旅人們許下最後一個願望。他們渴望的不只是高分，而是一個充滿好奇心的人生：持續閱讀、持續發問，也持續仰望。今晚過後很久，星星依然會閃耀，他們學過的每一個單字也是如此。他們明白，這座塔並不象徵道路的終點，而是一個讓人看清這條路能延伸多遠的地方。

questions.stem: What is the main message of the passage?
options: The Andromeda Galaxy is the most beautiful sight in the night sky.
High scores are the most important reason to learn words.
Learning, like climbing the tower, is a journey that continues beyond any single goal.
The travelers regret leaving home for such a long trip.
questions.explain: 文章以登上星空高塔比喻學習的旅程，並說登頂不代表旅程結束，塔是讓人看清道路能延伸多遠的地方，故選 (C)。(B) 文中說旅人渴望的不只是高分。
questions.evidence: The tower, they realize, does not symbolize the end of the road.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, when did the light we now see from the Andromeda Galaxy start its journey?
options: About two and a half thousand years ago
About two and a half million years ago
At the moment the travelers looked up
questions.explain: 第二段說仙女座星系的光大約在兩百五十萬年前就踏上旅程，故選 (B)。(A) 把「百萬」誤成「千」。
questions.evidence: Its light began its trek about two and a half million years ago

questions.stem: Why does the writer compare words to stars?
options: Both are hard to see in big cities.
Both last only a short time.
Both seem small alone but form meaningful patterns together.
questions.explain: 第三段說每個單字起初只是一個小光點，但單字和星星一樣很少單獨出現，會連成圖案，讓句子充滿意義，故選 (D)。其他選項文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: But words, like stars, are rarely seen alone. Together they form patterns

questions.stem: In paragraph 4, what does "they" in "When they come" refer to?
questions.explain: 前一句提到「也許會有混亂與懷疑的時刻」，接著說「當它們來臨時」，旅人可以想想自己爬了多高，所以 they 指混亂與懷疑的時刻，故選 (A)。(B) 旅人是後半句的主詞，不是「來臨」的東西。
questions.evidence: There may be moments of turmoil and doubt. When they come

vocab.stem: After decades of working in the sun, the old fisherman's face was covered with deep ______.
vocab.explain: 長年在陽光下工作，臉上布滿深深的「皺紋」，故選 wrinkles。walnuts（核桃）、vowels（母音）、wards（病房）都不會出現在臉上。

vocab.stem: Having grown up in the mountains, Lily had long ______ to see the ocean with her own eyes.
vocab.explain: 在山裡長大的莉莉一直「渴望」親眼看看大海，yearn to V 表示渴望做某事，故選 yearned。wrestled（摔角；搏鬥）、withheld（保留；扣留）、zoomed（急速移動）都不能接 to see 表達心願。
